sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十九】 起玄黓閹茂，盡昭陽大淵獻正月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 79] From Xuanmao through the first month of Dayuanyuan; in all, a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 79] From the cyclical year Xuanmao through the first month of Dayuanyuan—a span of somewhat more than one year.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝中之下天復二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Brilliant, and Cultured Filial, middle section, second part—Tianfu year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Brilliant, and Cultured Filial, middle section, second part—Tianfu year 2 (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元九零二年）

translations.literal: renxu cycle, corresponding to the year 902 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renxu cycle, corresponding to 902 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑，朱全忠復屯三原，又移軍武功。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guichou day, Zhu Quanzhong again encamped at Sanyuan and also shifted his army to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on guichou day, Zhu Quanzhong encamped again at Sanyuan and then moved his forces to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 河東將李嗣昭、周德威攻慈、隰，以分全忠兵勢。

translations.literal: The Hedong generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei attacked Ci and Xi to divide Quanzhong's military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei attacked Ci and Xi to draw off part of Quanzhong's forces.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以給事中韋貽范為工部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingmao day, Secretariat Drafter Wei Yifan was appointed Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day, Wei Yifan, a Secretariat drafter, was appointed vice minister of works and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以給事中嚴龜充岐、汴和協使，賜朱全忠姓李，與李茂貞為兄弟，全忠不從。

translations.literal: On bingzi day, Secretariat Drafter Yan Gui was made envoy for peace between Qi and Bian; Zhu Quanzhong was granted the surname Li and made a sworn brother of Li Maozhen; Quanzhong did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, Yan Gui, a Secretariat drafter, was appointed envoy to mediate peace between Qi and Bian; Zhu Quanzhong was granted the imperial surname Li and made a sworn brother of Li Maozhen, but Quanzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 時茂貞不出戰。

translations.literal: At that time Maozhen did not come out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Maozhen would not take the field.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞有河東兵，二月，戊寅朔，旋軍河中。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard there were Hedong troops; in the second month, on the wuyin new moon, he turned his army back to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong learned that Hedong forces were in the field, in the second month, on the wuyin new moon, he marched his army back to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭等攻慈、隰，下之，進逼晉、絳。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao and the others attacked Ci and Xi, took them, and pressed on toward Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao and his colleagues captured Ci and Xi and then advanced against Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 己丑，全忠遣兄子友寧將兵會晉州刺史氏叔琮擊之。

translations.literal: On jichou day, Quanzhong sent his elder brother's son Youning to lead troops and join Jinzhou prefect Shi Shuzong in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day, Quanzhong dispatched his nephew Youning with troops to join Jinzhou prefect Shi Shuzong in striking them.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭襲取絳州，汴將康懷英復取之。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao raided and took Jiangzhou; the Bian general Kang Huaiying retook it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao seized Jiangzhou by surprise, but Bian general Kang Huaiying recovered it.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭等屯蒲縣。

translations.literal: Sizhao and the others encamped at Pu County.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao and his forces encamped at Pu County.

sentences.zh: 乙未，汴軍十萬營於蒲南，叔琮夜帥眾斷其歸路而攻其壘，破之，殺獲萬餘人。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, a hundred thousand Bian troops camped south of Pu; at night Shuzong led his men to cut off their line of retreat and attack their camp, broke them, and killed or captured more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, one hundred thousand Bian troops encamped south of Pu; that night Shuzong led his men to sever their retreat and storm their camp, routing them and killing or capturing more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 己亥，全忠自河中赴之，乙巳，至晉州。

translations.literal: On jihai day, Quanzhong himself went from Hezhong to their aid; on yisi day he reached Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, Quanzhong marched from Hezhong to reinforce them; on yisi day he arrived at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜發簡陵。

translations.literal: Robbers excavated Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb robbers broke into Jianling.

sentences.zh: 西川兵至利州，昭武節度使李繼忠棄鎮奔鳳翔。

translations.literal: Xichuan troops reached Lizhou; Zhaowu military governor Li Jizhong abandoned his post and fled to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan forces reached Lizhou; Zhaowu military governor Li Jizhong abandoned his command and fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 王建以劍州刺史王宗偉為利州制置使。

translations.literal: Wang Jian appointed Jianzhou prefect Wang Zongwei as Lizhou system-making commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian appointed Jianzhou prefect Wang Zongwei commissioner for the Lizhou pacification command.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，上與李茂貞及宰相、學士、中尉、樞密宴，酒酣，茂貞及韓全誨亡去。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengxu day, the emperor banqueted with Li Maozhen and the chief ministers, scholars, palace commissioners, and Privy Council officials; when the wine had gone deep, Maozhen and Han Quanhui fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengxu day, the emperor held a banquet with Li Maozhen, the chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, palace commissioners, and Privy Council officials; when they were well into their cups, Maozhen and Han Quanhui slipped away.

sentences.zh: 上問韋貽范：「朕何以巡幸至此？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wei Yifan: "Why have I come on this tour to this place?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Yifan, "Why have I been brought on this imperial progress to such a place?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣在外不知。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant was outside and does not know."
translations.idiomatic: Yifan answered, "Your servant was away from court and does not know."

sentences.zh: 固問之，不對。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him repeatedly; he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him again and again, but he would not reply.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿何得於朕前妄語雲不知？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How dare you speak falsely before me and say you do not know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How dare you lie to my face and claim you do not know?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卿既以非道取宰相，當於公事如法，若有不可，必准故事。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Since you obtained the post of chief minister by improper means, you ought to handle public business according to law; if anything is not acceptable, you must follow precedent."
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "Since you gained the chief ministership by improper means, you ought to conduct state affairs by the book; where anything is inadmissible, you must follow established precedent."

sentences.zh: 怒目視之，微言曰：「此賊兼須杖之二十。」

translations.literal: He glared at him in anger and said under his breath: "This villain ought also to be beaten twenty strokes."
translations.idiomatic: Glaring at him in anger, he muttered, "This scoundrel deserves twenty strokes of the staff as well."

sentences.zh: 顧謂韓偓曰：「此輩亦稱宰相！」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to Han Wo: "These fellows also call themselves chief ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Han Wo, he said, "And these men still call themselves chief ministers!"

sentences.zh: 貽范屢以大杯獻上，上不即持，貽范舉杯直及上頤。

translations.literal: Yifan repeatedly offered the emperor large cups; the emperor did not take them at once, and Yifan raised his cup straight to the emperor's chin.
translations.idiomatic: Yifan kept pressing large cups on the emperor; when the emperor did not take one immediately, Yifan thrust the cup right up to his chin.

sentences.zh: 戊午，氏叔琮、朱友寧進攻李嗣昭、周德威營。

translations.literal: On wuwu day, Shi Shuzong and Zhu Youning advanced and attacked the camp of Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day, Shi Shuzong and Zhu Youning attacked the camp of Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei.

sentences.zh: 時汴軍橫陳十里，而河東軍不過數萬，深入敵境，眾心忷懼。

translations.literal: At that time the Bian army was drawn up for ten li, while the Hedong army numbered only a few tens of thousands; deep in enemy territory, the men's hearts were fearful and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian forces were deployed across ten li, while the Hedong army numbered only a few tens of thousands; deep inside enemy territory, the troops were anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 德威出戰而敗，密令嗣昭以後軍先去，德威尋引騎兵亦退。

translations.literal: Dewei went out to fight and was defeated; he secretly ordered Sizhao to take the rear guard and go ahead first, and Dewei soon led the cavalry in retreat as well.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei gave battle and was beaten; he secretly ordered Sizhao to withdraw with the rear guard first, and Dewei soon led the cavalry away as well.

sentences.zh: 叔琮、友寧長驅乘之，河東軍驚潰，禽克用子廷鸞，兵仗輜重委棄略盡。

translations.literal: Shuzong and Youning pursued at full speed; the Hedong army broke in panic, Keyong's son Tingluan was captured, and weapons, baggage, and transport were abandoned almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzong and Youning pressed the pursuit; the Hedong army collapsed in panic, Keyong's son Tingluan was taken prisoner, and arms, baggage, and transport were abandoned almost to the last item.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠令叔琮、友寧乘勝遂攻河東。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong ordered Shuzong and Youning to press their victory and attack Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong ordered Shuzong and Youning to follow up their victory with an invasion of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 李克用聞嗣昭等敗，遣李存信以親兵逆之，至清源，遇汴軍，存信走還晉陽。

translations.literal: When Li Keyong heard that Sizhao and the others had been defeated, he sent Li Cunxin with his personal troops to meet them; at Qingyuan they encountered Bian troops, and Cunxin fled back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong learned of Sizhao's defeat, he sent Li Cunxin with his personal guard to meet the retreat; at Qingyuan they ran into Bian forces, and Cunxin fled back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 汴軍取慈、隰、汾三州。

translations.literal: The Bian army took the three prefectures of Ci, Xi, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army captured the three prefectures of Ci, Xi, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，汴軍圍晉陽，營於晉祠，攻其西門。

translations.literal: On xinyou day, the Bian army besieged Jinyang, encamped at Jinci, and attacked the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, the Bian army laid siege to Jinyang, encamped at Jinci, and assaulted the west gate.

sentences.zh: 周德威、李嗣昭收餘眾依西山得還。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao gathered the survivors, followed the Western Hills, and were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao rallied the survivors along the Western Hills and made their way back.

sentences.zh: 城中兵未集，叔琮攻城甚急，每行圍，褒衣博帶，以示閒暇。

translations.literal: The troops in the city were not yet assembled; Shuzong pressed the siege very hard, yet whenever he walked the perimeter he wore loose robes with a broad belt to show leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The city's defenders were not yet fully mustered; Shuzong pressed the assault relentlessly, yet whenever he inspected the siege lines he wore loose robes and a broad belt to affect ease.

sentences.zh: 克用晝夜乘城，不得寢食。

translations.literal: Keyong day and night manned the walls and could neither sleep nor eat.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong spent day and night on the walls and could neither sleep nor eat.

sentences.zh: 召諸將議走保雲州，李嗣昭、李嗣源、周德威曰：「兒輩在此，必能固守。

translations.literal: He summoned the generals to discuss abandoning the city and holding Yunzhou; Li Sizhao, Li Siyuan, and Zhou Dewei said: "We your sons are here and can surely hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned his generals to discuss fleeing to Yunzhou; Li Sizhao, Li Siyuan, and Zhou Dewei said, "We are here, and we can surely hold the city.

sentences.zh: 王勿為此謀搖人心！」

translations.literal: My lord, do not entertain this plan and shake men's hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: My lord, do not entertain such a plan and unsettle the troops!"

sentences.zh: 李存信曰：「關東、河北皆受制於朱溫，我兵寡地蹙，守此孤城，彼築壘穿塹環之，以積久制我，我飛走無路，坐待困斃耳。

translations.literal: Li Cunxin said: "Guandong and Hebei are all subject to Zhu Wen; our troops are few and our territory cramped; holding this lone city, they will build ramparts and dig trenches to ring us, and in time wear us down—we have no way to flee by flight and can only sit and await exhaustion and death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin said, "Guandong and Hebei are all under Zhu Wen's thumb; our forces are few and our territory cramped. If we hold this lone city while they ring us with ramparts and trenches, they will wear us down in time. We have no escape—we can only sit here until we are spent.

sentences.zh: 今事勢已急，不若且入北虜，徐圖進取。」

translations.literal: The situation is already urgent; better for now to enter the northern barbarians and plan advance later."
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is upon us. Better to withdraw for now among the northern tribes and plan our comeback later."

sentences.zh: 嗣昭力爭之，克用不能決。

translations.literal: Sizhao argued against it strenuously, and Keyong could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao argued fiercely against it, and Keyong could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 劉夫人言於克用曰：「存信，北川牧羊兒耳，安知遠慮！

translations.literal: Lady Liu said to Keyong: "Cunxin is a sheepherding boy from the northern valleys—how would he know far-reaching plans!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu said to Keyong, "Cunxin is a shepherd boy from the northern valleys—what does he know of long-range strategy!

sentences.zh: 王常笑王行瑜輕去其城，死於人手，今日反效之邪！

translations.literal: My lord often laughed at Wang Xingyu for lightly abandoning his city and dying at others' hands—will you today imitate him!
translations.idiomatic: You yourself used to mock Wang Xingyu for lightly abandoning his city and dying at another's hands—will you now do the same!

sentences.zh: 且王昔居達靼，幾不自免。

translations.literal: Moreover, when my lord once lived among the Tatars, you nearly did not escape with your life.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when you once lived among the Tatars, you nearly lost your life.

sentences.zh: 賴朝廷多事，乃得復歸。

translations.literal: It was only because the court had many troubles that you were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the court was beset with troubles were you able to come home.

sentences.zh: 今一足出城，則禍變不測，塞外可得至邪！」

translations.literal: Now if one foot leaves the city, disaster will change unpredictably—how can you reach the lands beyond the passes!"
translations.idiomatic: If even one foot steps outside the walls now, disaster may strike without warning—how can you hope to reach the steppe at all!"

sentences.zh: 克用乃止。

translations.literal: Keyong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 居數日，潰兵復集，軍府浸安。

translations.literal: After several days, scattered troops gathered again, and the military headquarters gradually grew secure.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days scattered troops rallied again, and the headquarters gradually regained its footing.

sentences.zh: 克用弟克寧為忻州刺史，聞汴寇至，中塗復還晉陽，曰：「此城吾死所也，去將何之！」

translations.literal: Keyong's younger brother Kening was prefect of Xinzhou; hearing that Bian invaders had come, he turned back halfway and returned to Jinyang, saying: "This city is where I shall die—where would I go if I left!"
translations.idiomatic: Keyong's younger brother Kening, prefect of Xinzhou, heard that Bian forces were at hand, turned back midway, and returned to Jinyang, saying, "This city is where I die—where else would I go!"

sentences.zh: 眾心乃定。

translations.literal: The hearts of the multitude were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops' morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，朱全忠還河中，遣朱友寧將兵西擊李茂貞，軍於興平、武功之間。

translations.literal: On renxu day, Zhu Quanzhong returned to Hezhong and sent Zhu Youning to lead troops west to attack Li Maozhen, encamping between Xingping and Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day, Zhu Quanzhong returned to Hezhong and sent Zhu Youning west against Li Maozhen, encamping between Xingping and Wugong.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭、李嗣源數將敢死士夜入氏叔琮營，斬首捕虜，汴軍驚擾，備御不暇。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan several times led dare-to-die troops by night into Shi Shuzong's camp, beheading and capturing; the Bian army was alarmed and thrown into disorder and could not attend to defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan repeatedly led suicide squads by night into Shi Shuzong's camp, killing and taking prisoners; the Bian troops were thrown into alarm and could not keep their defenses in order.

sentences.zh: 會大疫，丁卯，叔琮引兵還。

translations.literal: A great epidemic occurred; on dingmao day, Shuzong led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: A severe epidemic broke out; on dingmao day, Shuzong withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭與周德威將兵追之，及石會關，叔琮留數馬及旌旗於高岡之巔。

translations.literal: Sizhao and Zhou Dewei led troops in pursuit; reaching Shihui Pass, Shuzong left several horses and banners on the summit of a high ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao and Zhou Dewei pursued; at Shihui Pass, Shuzong left a few horses and banners on a high ridge.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭等以為有伏兵，乃引去，復取慈、隰、汾三州。

translations.literal: Sizhao and the others thought there was an ambush and therefore withdrew, and again took the three prefectures of Ci, Xi, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao and his men took this for an ambush and withdrew, then recovered the three prefectures of Ci, Xi, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 自是克用不敢與全忠爭者累年。

translations.literal: From this time Keyong did not dare contend with Quanzhong for many years.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Keyong did not dare contest Quanzhong for many years.

sentences.zh: 克用以使引咨幕府曰：「不貯軍食，何以聚眾？

translations.literal: Keyong sent envoys to consult the staff headquarters, saying: "Without storing military grain, how can one gather the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent envoys to consult his staff headquarters, saying, "Without stockpiling military grain, how can we gather troops?

sentences.zh: 不置兵甲，何以克敵？

translations.literal: Without setting out arms and armor, how can one defeat the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Without equipping arms and armor, how can we defeat the enemy?

sentences.zh: 不修城池，何以扞御？

translations.literal: Without repairing city walls, how can one defend and resist?
translations.idiomatic: Without repairing the walls, how can we defend ourselves?

sentences.zh: 利害之間，請垂議度。」

translations.literal: Between benefit and harm, please bestow your deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Between benefit and harm, please give us your counsel."

sentences.zh: 掌書記李襲吉獻議，略曰：「國富不在倉儲，兵強不由眾寡，人歸有德，神固害盈。

translations.literal: Chief secretary Li Xiji submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "A state's wealth lies not in granaries; military strength does not depend on numbers large or small; people return to the virtuous, and the spirits indeed harm the full.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Li Xiji submitted a memorial that, in summary, said, "A state's wealth does not lie in its granaries; military strength does not depend on numbers alone; the people rally to virtue, and the spirits punish excess.

sentences.zh: 聚斂寧有盜臣，苛政有如猛虎，所以鹿台將散，周武以興；

translations.literal: Excessive levying surely produces thieving ministers; harsh government is like a fierce tiger—therefore when Lutai was about to scatter, King Wu of Zhou rose;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy exactions breed corrupt officials; harsh government is like a ravening tiger—thus when Lutai was about to fall, King Wu of Zhou rose up;

sentences.zh: 齊庫既焚，晏嬰入賀。」

translations.literal: when Qi's treasuries were burned, Yan Ying entered to congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: when Qi's treasuries burned, Yan Ying came in to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伏以變法不若養人，改作何如舊貫！

translations.literal: He also said: "I venture to say that changing the laws is not as good as nurturing the people; what is the use of new measures compared with the old ways!
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "I submit that changing the laws is inferior to nurturing the people—what good are innovations compared with established practice!

sentences.zh: 韓建蓄財無數，首事朱溫；

translations.literal: Han Jian amassed wealth beyond counting and was the first to serve Zhu Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian hoarded untold wealth and was the first to throw in with Zhu Wen;

sentences.zh: 王珂變法如麻，一朝降賊；

translations.literal: Wang Ke changed laws like hemp fibers and in one morning surrendered to the bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke changed laws at every turn and in a single morning surrendered to the rebels;

sentences.zh: 中山城非不峻，蔡上兵非不多；

translations.literal: Zhongshan's walls were not un-lofty, and Cai Shang's troops were not few;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan's walls were not low, and Cai Shang's troops were not few;

sentences.zh: 前事甚明，可以為戒。

translations.literal: the earlier cases are very clear and may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: these recent examples are plain enough to serve as warnings.

sentences.zh: 且霸國無貧主，強將無弱兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, a hegemonic state has no impoverished ruler, and a strong general has no weak soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a hegemonic state has no impoverished ruler, and a strong commander has no weak troops.

sentences.zh: 伏願大王崇德愛人，去奢省役，設險固境，訓兵務農。

translations.literal: I venture to hope that the great king will honor virtue and love the people, remove extravagance and reduce corvée, establish defenses and secure the borders, train troops and attend to agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to hope that Your Highness will honor virtue and cherish the people, cut extravagance and lighten corvée, fortify the borders, drill the army, and encourage farming.

sentences.zh: 定亂者選武臣，制理者選文吏，錢穀有句，刑法有律。

translations.literal: For settling disorder choose military officials; for governing choose civil officials; funds and grain have their accounts; punishments and laws have their statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Choose military men to quell disorder and civil officials to govern; keep clear accounts for revenue and grain, and fixed statutes for punishments and law.

sentences.zh: 誅賞由我，則下無威福之弊；

translations.literal: If rewards and punishments proceed from me, then below there will be no abuse of authority and favor;
translations.idiomatic: If rewards and punishments rest with you alone, subordinates cannot usurp authority;

sentences.zh: 近密多正，則人無譖謗之憂。

translations.literal: if those near and intimate are mostly upright, then people will have no worry of slander.
translations.idiomatic: if those close at hand are upright, the people need not fear slander.

sentences.zh: 順天時而絕欺誣，敬鬼神而禁淫祀；

translations.literal: Obey heaven's seasons and cut off deceit; revere ghosts and spirits and forbid improper sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Follow heaven's seasons and root out deceit; honor the spirits and forbid improper sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 則不求富而國富，不求安而自安。

translations.literal: then without seeking wealth the state will be wealthy, without seeking security it will be secure of itself.
translations.idiomatic: then without seeking wealth the state will grow rich, and without seeking peace it will find peace.

sentences.zh: 外破元兇，內康疲俗，名高五霸，道冠八元。

translations.literal: Without, break the arch-criminal; within, bring ease to the weary populace—your fame will rise above the Five Hegemons, your Way crown the Eight Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Destroy the arch-enemy abroad and bring ease to a weary people at home—your fame will surpass the Five Hegemons and your Way outshine the Eight Worthies.

sentences.zh: 至於率閭閻，定間架，增曲薛，檢田疇，開國建邦，恐未為切。」

translations.literal: As for leading the lanes and wards, fixing the jianjia tax frames, increasing the quxue levies, and inspecting fields—founding a state and establishing a dynasty— I fear these are not yet urgent."
translations.idiomatic: As for surveying households, fixing tax brackets, increasing surcharges, and inspecting fields—founding a state and establishing a dynasty—these, I fear, are not yet the urgent tasks."

sentences.zh: 克用親軍皆沙陀雜虜，喜侵暴良民，河東甚苦之。

translations.literal: Keyong's personal army were all Shatuo and mixed barbarians who delighted in invading and oppressing good common people; Hedong suffered greatly from them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong's personal troops were Shatuo and other tribal auxiliaries who preyed on the common people; Hedong suffered greatly under them.

sentences.zh: 其子存勖以為言，克用曰：「此輩從吾攻戰數十年，比者帑藏空虛，諸軍賣馬以自給。

translations.literal: His son Cunxu spoke of it; Keyong said: "These fellows have followed me in attack and battle for several decades; recently the treasury has been empty, and the various armies sell horses to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cunxu raised the matter; Keyong said, "These men have fought beside me for decades. Lately the treasury has been empty and the armies have had to sell their horses to live.

sentences.zh: 今四方諸侯皆重賞以募士，我若急之，則彼皆散去矣，吾安與同保此乎！

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords in all directions use heavy rewards to recruit soldiers; if I press them hard, they will all scatter—how could I together with them preserve this!
translations.idiomatic: Every warlord now offers rich rewards to recruit men. If I crack down on them, they will all desert—how could I hold this place with them!

sentences.zh: 俟天下稍平，當更清治之耳。」

translations.literal: When the realm is somewhat at peace, I shall clean them up again."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm settles a little, I will set things right again."

sentences.zh: 存勖幼警敏，有勇略，克用為朱全忠所困，封疆日蹙，憂形於色。

translations.literal: Cunxu in youth was keen and quick, with courage and strategy; Keyong was hemmed in by Zhu Quanzhong, his territory daily shrinking, and worry showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu had been clever and bold from boyhood. Hemmed in by Zhu Quanzhong, Keyong watched his domain shrink day by day, and his worry showed plainly.

sentences.zh: 存勖進言曰：「物不極則不返，惡不極則不亡。

translations.literal: Cunxu advanced and said: "When things do not reach the extreme they do not turn back; when evil does not reach the extreme it does not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu spoke up: "Things that do not reach an extreme do not turn back; evil that does not reach an extreme does not perish.

sentences.zh: 朱氏恃其詐力，窮凶極暴，吞滅四鄰，人怨神怒。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan relies on its deceit and force, exhausts villainy and utmost violence, swallows and destroys its neighbors on four sides—people resent and spirits are angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu clan trusts in deceit and brute force, has run to the utmost in cruelty, swallowed its neighbors on every side, and earned the hatred of men and the wrath of heaven.

sentences.zh: 今又攻逼乘輿，窺覦神器，此其極也，殆將斃矣！

translations.literal: Now again they attack and press the imperial carriage and covet the sacred regalia—this is their extreme; they will soon be at their end!
translations.idiomatic: Now they press the imperial carriage and covet the throne itself—this is their extreme; they are near their end!

sentences.zh: 吾家代襲忠貞，勢窮力屈，無所愧心。

translations.literal: Our house has for generations inherited loyalty and steadfastness; though power is exhausted and strength bent, we have nothing for which to feel ashamed in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has served in loyalty for generations. Though we are spent in strength, we have nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 大人當遵養時晦以待其衰，奈何輕為沮喪，使群下失望乎！」

translations.literal: My lord ought to nurture your strength in obscurity and await their decline—why lightly give way to dejection and make your subordinates lose hope!
translations.idiomatic: Father, you should bide your time in quiet strength and wait for their decline—why let yourself sink into despair and disappoint those below you!

sentences.zh: 克用悅，即命酒奏樂而罷。

translations.literal: Keyong was pleased and at once ordered wine and had music played, then dismissed the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was pleased, ordered wine, had music played, and dismissed the gathering.

sentences.zh: 劉夫人無子，克用寵姬曹氏生存勖，劉夫人待曹氏加厚。

translations.literal: Lady Liu had no son; Keyong's favored concubine Lady Cao bore Cunxu, and Lady Liu treated Lady Cao with added generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu had no children; Keyong's favored concubine Lady Cao bore Cunxu, and Lady Liu treated Lady Cao with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 克用以是益賢之，諸姬有子，輒命夫人母之。

translations.literal: Keyong for this reason esteemed her all the more; whenever any concubine bore a son, he would order the lady to be mother to the child.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong esteemed her all the more for this; whenever a concubine bore a son, he charged Lady Liu to raise the child as her own.

sentences.zh: 夫人教養，悉如所生。

translations.literal: The lady reared and taught them all exactly as if they were her own.
translations.idiomatic: She reared and taught each one exactly as if he were her own.

sentences.zh: 上以左金吾將軍李儼為江、淮宣諭使，書御衣賜楊行密，拜行密東面行營都統、中書令、吳王，以討朱全忠。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Left Golden Guards General Li Yan as envoy to proclaim and instruct on the Jiang and Huai, wrote on imperial robes and granted them to Yang Xingmi, and appointed Xingmi eastern campaign commander-in-chief, Secretariat Director, and King of Wu, to attack Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Left Golden Guards General Li Yan envoy to proclaim the court's will in the Jiang and Huai regions, wrote on imperial robes and bestowed them on Yang Xingmi, and named him eastern campaign commander-in-chief, Secretariat director, and King of Wu to campaign against Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 以朱瑾為平盧節度使，馮弘鐸為武寧節度使，朱延壽為奉國節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin was made Pinglu military governor, Feng Hongduo Wuning military governor, and Zhu Yanshou Fengguo military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin was appointed military governor of Pinglu, Feng Hongduo of Wuning, and Zhu Yanshou of Fengguo.

sentences.zh: 加武安節度使馬殷同平章事。

translations.literal: Wuan military governor Ma Yin was additionally made Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin, military governor of Wuan, was additionally appointed associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 淮南、宣歙、湖南等道立功將士，聽用都統牒承製遷補，然後表聞。

translations.literal: Meritorious officers and soldiers of Huainan, Xuanshe, Hunan, and other circuits who had earned distinction were permitted to be promoted and reassigned by the commander's-in-chief's warrant in accordance with imperial appointment, and then reported in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officers and soldiers of Huainan, Xuanshe, Hunan, and other circuits might be promoted and reassigned on the commander's warrant in accordance with imperial procedure, with memorials to follow.

sentences.zh: 儼，張濬之子也，賜姓李。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of Zhang Jun and had been granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the son of Zhang Jun and had been granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁酉，崔胤自華州詣河中，泣訴於朱全忠，恐李茂貞劫天子幸蜀，宜以時迎奉，勢不可緩。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou day, Cui Yin went from Huazhou to Hezhong and tearfully appealed to Zhu Quanzhong, fearing that Li Maozhen would seize the Son of Heaven and take him to Shu; he ought to welcome and attend him in good time—the situation could not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on dingyou day, Cui Yin went from Huazhou to Hezhong and tearfully pleaded with Zhu Quanzhong, fearing that Li Maozhen would seize the emperor and take him to Shu; the emperor should be welcomed back to the capital without delay—the moment would not wait.

sentences.zh: 全忠與之宴，胤親執板，為全忠歌以侑酒。

translations.literal: Quanzhong banqueted with him; Yin personally held the clappers and sang for Quanzhong to accompany the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong feasted with him; Yin himself beat time and sang to enliven the drinking.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，回鶻遣使入貢，請發兵赴難，上命翰林學士承旨韓偓答書許之。

translations.literal: On xinchou day, the Uyghurs sent envoys to offer tribute and requested troops to come to the realm's aid; the emperor ordered Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Han Wo to reply in writing granting it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day, the Uyghurs sent tribute envoys asking that troops be sent to the court's aid; the emperor ordered Hanlin academician-in-chief Han Wo to reply granting the request.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，偓上言：「戎狄獸心，不可倚信。

translations.literal: On yisi day, Wo submitted a memorial: "The Rong and Di have the hearts of beasts and cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day, Wo memorialized, "The northern tribes have the hearts of beasts and cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 彼見國家人物華靡，而城邑荒殘，甲兵雕弊，必有輕中國之心，啟其貪婪。

translations.literal: They see the state's people and things splendid and extravagant, while cities and towns are desolate and ruined and arms and armor worn out—they will surely have hearts that belittle China and will awaken their greed.
translations.idiomatic: They will see our splendor beside ruined cities and broken armies, and will surely despise China and give free rein to their greed.

sentences.zh: 且自會昌以來，回鶻為中國所破，恐其乘危復怨。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the Huichang era the Uyghurs have been broken by China—they may fear that, seizing our peril, they will renew their resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Huichang the Uyghurs have been broken by China; they may seize our weakness to settle old scores.

sentences.zh: 所賜可汗書，宜諭以小小寇竊，不須赴難，虛愧其意，實沮其謀。」

translations.literal: In the letter granted to the qaghan, he should be instructed that petty bandits and thieves are at work and there is no need to come to the aid; outwardly to shame their intent, but in fact to thwart their scheme."
translations.idiomatic: The letter to the qaghan should explain that only petty raiders are abroad and no expedition is needed—outwardly to spare their pride, but in fact to block their design."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎參知機務盧光啟罷為太子太保。

translations.literal: Minister of War and participant in state affairs Lu Guangqi was removed and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangqi, vice minister of war and participant in state affairs, was dismissed and appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣顧全武歸杭州以易秦裴，錢鏐大喜，遣裴還。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Gu Quanwu back to Hangzhou in exchange for Qin Pei; Qian Liu was greatly pleased and sent Pei back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi returned Gu Quanwu to Hangzhou in exchange for Qin Pei; Qian Liu was delighted and sent Pei back.

sentences.zh: 汴將康懷貞擊鳳翔將李繼昭於莫谷，大破之。

translations.literal: The Bian general Kang Huaizhen attacked the Fengxiang general Li Jizhao at Mogu and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Kang Huaizhen attacked Fengxiang general Li Jizhao at Mogu and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 繼昭，蔡州人也，本姓苻，名道昭。

translations.literal: Jizhao was a man of Caizhou; his original surname was Fu and his name Daozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhao was from Caizhou; his original surname was Fu and his given name Daozhao.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚戌，溫州刺史朱褒卒，兄敖自稱刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengxu day, Wenzhou prefect Zhu Bao died; his elder brother Ao declared himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengxu day, Wenzhou prefect Zhu Bao died; his elder brother Ao proclaimed himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔人聞朱全忠且來，皆懼，癸丑，城外居民皆遷入城。

translations.literal: When the people of Fengxiang heard that Zhu Quanzhong was about to come, all were afraid; on guichou day, residents outside the walls all moved into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengxiang learned that Zhu Quanzhong was coming, everyone was afraid; on guichou day, residents outside the walls all moved into the city.

sentences.zh: 己未，全忠將精兵五萬發河中，至東渭橋，遇霖雨，留旬日。

translations.literal: On jiwei day, Quanzhong led fifty thousand picked troops out from Hezhong, reached Dongwei Bridge, encountered prolonged rain, and stayed ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day, Quanzhong marched fifty thousand elite troops from Hezhong to Dongwei Bridge, where heavy rains detained him for ten days.

sentences.zh: 庚午，工部侍郎、同平章事韋貽范遭母喪，宦官薦翰林學士姚洎為相。

translations.literal: On gengwu day, Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister Wei Yifan entered mourning for his mother; eunuchs recommended Hanlin Academician Yao Ji for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, Wei Yifan, vice minister of works and associate chief minister, entered mourning for his mother; the eunuchs recommended Hanlin academician Yao Ji for chief minister.

sentences.zh: 洎謀於韓偓，偓曰：「若圖永久之利，則莫若未就為善；

translations.literal: Ji consulted Han Wo; Wo said: "If you seek lasting benefit, nothing is better than not taking the post in the first place;
translations.idiomatic: Ji consulted Han Wo, who said, "If you want lasting good, nothing beats not taking the post at all;

sentences.zh: 倘出上意，固無不可。

translations.literal: if it proceeds from the emperor's mind, then of course there is nothing impossible.
translations.idiomatic: if the appointment comes from the emperor himself, that is another matter.

sentences.zh: 且汴軍旦夕合圍，孤城難保，家族在東，可不慮乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Bian army will complete the encirclement any day now; this lone city will be hard to hold—your family is in the east; can you not be concerned!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Bian army will close the ring any day; this lone city cannot be held—and your family is in the east. Have you considered that?"

sentences.zh: 洎乃移疾，上亦自不許。

translations.literal: Ji then pleaded illness, and the emperor himself would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then pleaded illness, and the emperor himself refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 鎮海、鎮東節度使彭城王錢鏐進爵越王。

translations.literal: The Zhenhai and Zhendong military governor, Prince of Pengcheng Qian Liu, was advanced in rank to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong and prince of Pengcheng, was promoted to prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，以中書舍人蘇檢為工部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingzi day, Secretariat Drafter Su Jian was made Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi day, Su Jian, a Secretariat drafter, was appointed vice minister of works and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時韋貽范在草土，薦檢及姚洎於李茂貞。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Yifan was in the grass and earth of mourning and recommended Su Jian and Yao Ji to Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Yifan was in mourning and recommended Su Jian and Yao Ji to Li Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 上既不用洎，茂貞及宦官恐上自用人，協力薦檢，遂用之。

translations.literal: The emperor having not used Ji, Maozhen and the eunuchs feared the emperor would appoint men on his own; they joined forces to recommend Jian, and he was then appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor had refused Ji, Maozhen and the eunuchs feared he would choose his own ministers; they joined to push Jian through, and he was appointed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，朱全忠軍於虢縣。

translations.literal: On dingchou day, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Guo County.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使馮弘鐸介居宣、楊之間，常不自安，然自恃樓船之強，不事兩道。

translations.literal: Wuning military governor Feng Hongduo lay between Xuan and Yang and was often ill at ease, yet relying on the strength of his tower ships, he served neither circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hongduo of Wuning lay between the Xuanshe and Yang circuits and was never secure, yet trusting in his tower ships, he submitted to neither.

sentences.zh: 寧國節度使田頵欲圖之，募弘鐸工人造戰艦，工人曰：「馮公遠求堅木，故其船堪久用，今此無之。」

translations.literal: Ningguo military governor Tian Yun wished to destroy him and recruited Hongduo's craftsmen to build warships; the craftsmen said: "Lord Feng sought hard timber from afar, so his ships can last long use—here there is none."
translations.idiomatic: Ningguo military governor Tian Yun plotted against him and hired Hongduo's shipwrights to build warships; they said, "Lord Feng brought in hard timber from afar, so his ships last—there is none of that here."

sentences.zh: 頵曰：「第為之，吾止須一用耳。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "Just build them—I only need to use them once."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Build them anyway—I need them only once."

sentences.zh: 弘鐸將馮暉、顏建說弘鐸先擊頵，弘鐸從之，帥眾南上，聲言攻洪州，實襲宣州也。

translations.literal: Hongduo's generals Feng Hui and Yan Jian urged Hongduo to strike Yun first; Hongduo followed this, led his forces south, declared he would attack Hongzhou, but in fact raided Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongduo's generals Feng Hui and Yan Jian urged him to strike Yun first; he agreed, marched south claiming he would attack Hongzhou, but in fact aimed at Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密使人止之，不從。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent men to stop him; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent envoys to stop him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，頵帥舟師逆擊於葛山，大破之。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, Yun led his fleet to meet the attack at Geshan and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day, Yun met him with his fleet at Geshan and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 甲申，李茂貞大出兵，自將之，與朱全忠戰於虢縣之北，大敗而還，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: On jiashen day, Li Maozhen sent out a great army and personally commanded it; he fought Zhu Quanzhong north of Guo County, was utterly defeated and returned, and more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Li Maozhen led a great army in person against Zhu Quanzhong north of Guo County, was routed, and lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，全忠遣其將孔勍出散關攻鳳州，拔之。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, Quanzhong sent his general Kong Qing out through San Pass to attack Fengzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, Quanzhong sent his general Kong Qing through San Pass against Fengzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，全忠進軍鳳翔城下。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Quanzhong advanced his army beneath Fengxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Quanzhong marched to Fengxiang and camped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 全忠朝服向城而泣，曰：「臣但欲迎車駕還宮耳，不與岐王角勝也。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong in court dress faced the city and wept, saying: "Your servant only wishes to welcome the imperial carriage back to the palace—I do not contend for victory with the Prince of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, in court dress, faced the city and wept, saying, "I only wish to bring the imperial carriage home—I am not fighting the Prince of Qi for victory."

sentences.zh: 遂為五寨環之。

translations.literal: He then built five camps to ring the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then built five camps to encircle the city.

sentences.zh: 馮弘鐸收餘眾沿江將入海，楊行密恐其為後患，遣使犒軍，且說之曰：「公徒眾猶盛，胡為自棄滄海之外！

translations.literal: Feng Hongduo gathered his survivors and was about to go to sea along the river; Yang Xingmi feared he would become a later trouble and sent envoys to reward the army, also persuading him: "Your followers are still numerous—why abandon yourself beyond the blue sea!
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hongduo rallied his survivors and prepared to put to sea; Yang Xingmi, fearing future trouble, sent envoys with gifts and said, "Your force is still strong—why cast yourself beyond the sea?

sentences.zh: 吾府雖小，足以容公之眾，使將吏各得其所，如何？」

translations.literal: Though my prefecture is small, it is enough to hold your multitude and let officers and clerks each find their place—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: My domain is small, but large enough for your men, with a place for every officer—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 弘鐸左右皆慟哭聽命。

translations.literal: Hongduo's attendants all wept bitterly and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongduo's followers wept and submitted.

sentences.zh: 弘鐸至東塘，行密自乘輕舟迎之，從者十餘人，常服，不持兵，升弘鐸舟，慰諭之，舉軍感悅。

translations.literal: When Hongduo reached Dongtang, Xingmi himself took a light boat to meet him, with a little more than ten followers in ordinary dress, bearing no weapons; he boarded Hongduo's ship and comforted and instructed him—the whole army was moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongduo reached Dongtang, Xingmi rowed out in a light boat with only a dozen men in plain clothes and unarmed, boarded Hongduo's ship, and reassured him; the whole army was won over.

sentences.zh: 署弘鐸淮南節度副使，館給甚厚。

translations.literal: He appointed Hongduo deputy military governor of Huainan and lodged and supplied him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Hongduo deputy military governor of Huainan and treated him with lavish hospitality.

sentences.zh: 初，弘鐸遣牙將丹徒尚公乃詣行密求潤州，行密不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hongduo had sent his adjutant Shang Gongnai of Dantu to ask Xingmi for Runzhou, and Xingmi had refused.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hongduo had sent his adjutant Shang Gongnai of Dantu to ask Xingmi for Runzhou, and Xingmi had refused.

sentences.zh: 公乃大言曰：「公不見聽，但恐不敵樓船耳。」

translations.literal: Gong then spoke boldly: "If my lord will not heed us, I fear only that you cannot match our tower ships."
translations.idiomatic: Gong had blustered, "If you won't listen, I fear only that you cannot match our tower ships."

sentences.zh: 至是，行密謂公乃曰：「頗記求潤州時否？」

translations.literal: Now Xingmi said to Gong: "Do you quite remember when you sought Runzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Xingmi said to him, "Do you remember asking for Runzhou?"

sentences.zh: 公乃謝曰：「將吏各為其主，但恨無成耳。」

translations.literal: Gong then apologized: "Officers and clerks each serve their lord—we only regret that we did not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Gong apologized, "Officers serve their lords—we only regret that we failed."

sentences.zh: 行密笑曰：「爾事楊叟如馮公，無憂矣！」

translations.literal: Xingmi laughed and said: "If you serve old Yang as you did Lord Feng, you need have no worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi laughed and said, "Serve old Yang as you served Lord Feng, and you'll be fine!"

sentences.zh: 行密以李神福為升州刺史。

translations.literal: Xingmi appointed Li Shenfu prefect of Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi appointed Li Shenfu prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密發兵討朱全忠，以副使李承嗣權知淮南軍府事。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent troops to attack Zhu Quanzhong and had his deputy Li Chengsi act as provisional administrator of the Huainan military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi marched against Zhu Quanzhong and left his deputy Li Chengsi in charge of the Huainan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 軍吏欲以巨艦運糧，都知兵馬使徐溫曰：「運路久不行，葭葦堙塞，請用小艇，庶幾易通。」

translations.literal: The army officers wished to transport grain with great ships; Director of Military Affairs Xu Wen said: "The transport route has long gone unused and reeds and rushes have choked it—please use small boats, so that passage may perhaps be easy."
translations.idiomatic: The staff wanted to move grain in large ships; director of military affairs Xu Wen said, "The water route has long been unused and is choked with reeds—use small boats instead; they will get through more easily."

sentences.zh: 軍至宿州，會久雨，重載不能進，士有饑色，而小艇先至，行密由是奇溫，始與議軍事。

translations.literal: When the army reached Suzhou, prolonged rain occurred; heavy loads could not advance and the soldiers showed hunger; but the small boats arrived first, and Xingmi for this reason marveled at Wen and began to consult with him on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzhou prolonged rains stalled the heavy transports and the men grew hungry, while the small boats arrived first; Xingmi was impressed and began to consult Wen on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 行密攻宿州，久不克，竟以糧運不繼引還。

translations.literal: Xingmi attacked Suzhou but could not take it for a long time and in the end withdrew because grain transport could not continue.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi besieged Suzhou for a long time without success and finally withdrew when supplies failed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，孔勍取成、隴二州，士卒無斗者。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Kong Qing took the two prefectures of Cheng and Long; not a soldier fought.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Kong Qing took Cheng and Long; not a man resisted.

sentences.zh: 至秦州，州人城守，乃自故關歸。

translations.literal: Reaching Qinzhou, the people of the prefecture walled and defended it, and he therefore returned by the old pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzhou the people held the walls, so he turned back by the old pass.

sentences.zh: 韋貽范之為相也，多受人賂，許以官。

translations.literal: When Wei Yifan was chief minister, he accepted many bribes from people and promised them offices.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Wei Yifan took many bribes and promised offices in return.

sentences.zh: 既而以母喪罷去，日為債家所噪。

translations.literal: Afterward he left office on his mother's death and daily was clamored at by creditors.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office for his mother's mourning, creditors hounded him daily.

sentences.zh: 親吏劉延美，所負尤多，故汲汲於起復，日遣人詣兩中尉、樞密及李茂貞求之。

translations.literal: His personal clerk Liu Yanmei owed especially much, so he was urgently eager for recall from mourning and daily sent men to the two palace commissioners, the Privy Council, and Li Maozhen to seek it.
translations.idiomatic: His personal clerk Liu Yanmei was his heaviest creditor, so Yifan pressed desperately for recall from mourning, sending men daily to the palace commissioners, the Privy Council, and Li Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，命韓偓草貽范起複製，偓曰：「吾腕可斷，此制不可草！」

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, the emperor ordered Han Wo to draft the edict recalling Yifan from mourning; Wo said: "My wrist may be cut off, but this edict cannot be drafted!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day, the emperor ordered Han Wo to draft Yifan's recall from mourning; Wo said, "You may cut off my wrist, but I will not draft this edict!"

sentences.zh: 即上疏論貽范遭憂未數月，遽令起復，實駭物聽，傷國體。

translations.literal: He at once submitted a memorial arguing that Yifan had entered mourning only a few months before and to order him recalled so hastily would truly shock public opinion and harm the state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized that Yifan had been in mourning only a few months and that hasty recall would shock opinion and injure the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 學士院二中使怒曰：「學士勿以死為戲！」

translations.literal: The two palace commissioners in the Hanlin Academy were angry and said: "Academician, do not make a game of death!"
translations.idiomatic: The two palace commissioners at the Hanlin Academy snapped, "Academician, do not trifle with your life!"

sentences.zh: 偓以疏授之，解衣而寢，二使不得已奏之。

translations.literal: Wo handed them the memorial, removed his robe, and went to bed; the two commissioners had no choice but to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Wo handed them the memorial, undressed, and went to bed; the commissioners had no choice but to submit it.

sentences.zh: 上即命罷草，仍賜敕褒賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor at once ordered the drafting stopped and still granted an edict praising and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once canceled the draft and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥朔，班定，無白麻可宣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the yihai new moon, when the court session was set, there was no white hemp edict to proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the yihai new moon, when court assembled, there was no white hemp edict to proclaim.

sentences.zh: 宦官喧言韓侍郎不肯草麻，聞者大駭。

translations.literal: The eunuchs clamored that Vice Minister Han would not draft the hemp edict; those who heard were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs clamored that Vice Minister Han had refused to draft the edict, and the court was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 茂貞入見上曰：「陛下命相而學士不肯草麻，與反何異！」

translations.literal: Maozhen entered and saw the emperor, saying: "Your Majesty appoints a chief minister and the academician will not draft the hemp edict—how is this different from rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen went in and said, "Your Majesty appoints a chief minister, and the academician refuses to draft the edict—how is that different from rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿輩薦貽范，朕不之違，學士不草麻，朕亦不之違。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You recommended Yifan, and I did not go against it; the academician will not draft the hemp edict, and I also will not go against it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You recommended Yifan, and I did not refuse you; the academician will not draft the edict, and I will not force him either.

sentences.zh: 況彼所陳，事理明白，若之何不從！」

translations.literal: Moreover, what he set forth is clear in reason and fact—why should I not follow it!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what he argues is plainly right—why should I not heed it!"

sentences.zh: 茂貞不悅而出，至中書，見蘇檢曰：「奸邪朋黨，宛然如舊。」

translations.literal: Maozhen left displeased, went to the Secretariat, and said to Su Jian: "Wicked and treacherous cliques are just as before."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen left in displeasure, went to the Secretariat, and told Su Jian, "The wicked cliques are just as they ever were."

sentences.zh: 扼腕者久之。

translations.literal: He wrung his wrists for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrung his hands for a long while.

sentences.zh: 貽范猶經營不已，茂貞語人曰：「我實不知書生禮數，為貽范所誤，會當於邠州安置。」

translations.literal: Yifan still schemed without cease; Maozhen told someone: "I truly did not know the bookish rites—Yifan misled me; when the time comes I shall settle him at Binzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Yifan kept scheming; Maozhen told someone, "I did not understand these scholar's rites—Yifan misled me. When the time comes I will park him at Binzhou."

sentences.zh: 貽范乃止。

translations.literal: Yifan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yifan then gave up.

sentences.zh: 劉延美赴井死。

translations.literal: Liu Yanmei threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanmei drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 保大節度使李茂勳將兵屯三原，救李茂貞。

translations.literal: Baoda military governor Li Maoxun led troops to encamp at Sanyuan to rescue Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Baoda military governor Li Maoxun encamped at Sanyuan with troops to relieve Li Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣其將康懷英、孔勍擊之，茂勳遁去。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent his generals Kang Huaiying and Kong Qing to attack him; Maoxun fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Kang Huaiying and Kong Qing against him, and Maoxun fled.

sentences.zh: 茂勳，茂貞之從弟也。

translations.literal: Maoxun was Maozhen's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun was Maozhen's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 初，孫儒死，其士卒多奔浙西，錢鏐愛其驍悍，以為中軍，號武勇都。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sun Ru died, many of his soldiers fled to western Zhe; Qian Liu admired their fierceness and made them the central army, styled the Martial Valor Command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sun Ru died, many of his soldiers fled to western Zhe; Qian Liu admired their fierceness, made them his central army, and called them the Martial Valor Command.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬杜稜諫曰：「狼子野心，他日必為深患，請以土人代之。」

translations.literal: Campaigning army marshal Du Ling remonstrated: "Wolf-cub hearts and wild-beast ambitions—they will surely become a deep trouble another day; please replace them with local men."
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning army marshal Du Ling warned, "They have the hearts of wolf cubs—one day they will be a grave danger. Replace them with local troops."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu refused.

sentences.zh: 鏐如衣錦軍，命武勇右都指揮使徐綰帥眾治溝洫；

translations.literal: Liu went to the Yijin army and ordered Xu Kuan, right commander of the Martial Valor Command, to lead the multitude in repairing ditches and canals;
translations.idiomatic: Liu went to the Yijin army and ordered Xu Kuan, right commander of the Martial Valor Command, to lead his men in digging ditches and canals;

sentences.zh: 鎮海節度副使成及聞士卒怨言，白鏐請罷役，不從。

translations.literal: Zhenhai deputy military governor Cheng Ji heard the soldiers' complaints of grievance and informed Liu, asking to stop the labor; he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai deputy military governor Cheng Ji heard the men's complaints and asked Liu to stop the work; Liu refused.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，鏐臨饗諸將，綰謀殺鏐於座，不果，稱疾先出。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, Liu personally feasted the generals; Xu Kuan plotted to kill Liu at the seat but did not succeed, and pleaded illness and left first.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, Liu feasted his generals; Xu Kuan plotted to kill him at table but failed, then pleaded illness and left early.

sentences.zh: 鏐怪之，丁亥，命綰將所部先還杭州。

translations.literal: Liu thought it strange; on dinghai day he ordered Xu Kuan to lead his command back to Hangzhou first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was suspicious; on dinghai day he ordered Xu Kuan to march his command back to Hangzhou ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 及外城，縱兵焚掠。

translations.literal: When they reached the outer city, he let his troops burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the city walls he turned his men loose to burn and plunder.

sentences.zh: 武勇左都指揮使許再思以迎侯兵與之合，進逼牙城。

translations.literal: Xu Zaisi, left commander of the Martial Valor Command, joined him with the welcoming escort troops, and they advanced to press the headquarters city.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zaisi, left commander of the Martial Valor Command, joined him with the escort troops and pressed the headquarters compound.

sentences.zh: 鏐子傳瑛與三城都指揮使馬綽等閉門拒之，牙將潘長擊綰，綰退屯龍興寺。

translations.literal: Liu's son Chuanying and the three-cities commander Ma Chuo and others shut the gates to resist them; adjutant Pan Chang attacked Xu Kuan, and Kuan withdrew to encamp at Longxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's son Chuanying, three-cities commander Ma Chuo, and others shut the gates to hold them off; adjutant Pan Chang struck Xu Kuan, who withdrew to Longxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 鏐還，及龍泉，聞變，疾驅至城北，使成及建鏐旗喜與綰戰，鏐微服乘小舟夜抵牙城東北隅，逾城而入。

translations.literal: Liu was returning; when he reached Longquan he heard of the revolt, galloped swiftly to the north of the city, and had Cheng Ji raise Liu's banner to engage Kuan in battle; Liu in plain dress took a small boat by night to the northeast corner of the headquarters city, climbed over the wall, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was on his way back; at Longquan he heard of the revolt, galloped to the north wall, and had Cheng Ji raise his banner and fight Kuan; Liu, in disguise, took a small boat by night to the northeast corner of the compound, scaled the wall, and entered.

sentences.zh: 直更卒憑鼓而寐，鏐親斬之，城中始知鏐至。

translations.literal: The night-watch soldier leaned on the drum and slept; Liu personally beheaded him, and only then did the city know Liu had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: A night watchman was asleep against the drum; Liu beheaded him himself, and only then did the city know he had returned.

sentences.zh: 武安都指揮使杜建徽自新城入援，徐綰聚木將焚北門，建徽悉焚之。

translations.literal: Wuan commander Du Jianhui entered from Xincheng to reinforce them; Xu Kuan gathered wood to burn the north gate, and Jianhui burned it all.
translations.idiomatic: Wuan commander Du Jianhui marched in from Xincheng to reinforce them; Xu Kuan piled wood to burn the north gate, and Jianhui burned the pile.

sentences.zh: 建徽，稜之子也。

translations.literal: Jianhui was Ling's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui was Du Ling's son.

sentences.zh: 湖州刺史高彥聞難，遣其子渭將兵入援，至靈隱山，綰伏兵擊殺之。

translations.literal: Huzhou prefect Gao Yan heard of the trouble and sent his son Wei with troops to reinforce them; reaching Lingyin Mountain, Kuan's ambush struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou prefect Gao Yan heard of the trouble and sent his son Wei with troops; at Lingyin Mountain, Kuan's ambush killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，鏐築杭州羅城，謂僚佐曰：「十步一樓，可以為固矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu built Hangzhou's outer wall, he told his aides: "A tower every ten paces—this can make it secure."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu built Hangzhou's outer wall, he told his staff, "A tower every ten paces will make it secure."

sentences.zh: 掌書記餘杭羅隱曰：「樓不若皆內向。」

translations.literal: Chief secretary Luo Yin of Yuhang said: "The towers would be better all facing inward."
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Luo Yin of Yuhang said, "Better build them all facing inward."

sentences.zh: 至是人以隱言為驗。

translations.literal: Now people took Yin's words as verified.
translations.idiomatic: Now people saw that Yin's advice had been proved right.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，李茂貞出兵夜襲奉天，虜汴將倪章、邵棠以歸。

translations.literal: On gengxu day, Li Maozhen sent troops by night to raid Fengtian and captured the Bian generals Ni Zhang and Shao Tang, bringing them back.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, Li Maozhen raided Fengtian by night and captured Bian generals Ni Zhang and Shao Tang.

sentences.zh: 乙未，茂貞大出兵，與朱全忠戰，不勝，暮歸，汴兵追之，幾入西門。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, Maozhen sent out a great army and fought Zhu Quanzhong but did not win; at evening he returned, Bian troops pursued, and they nearly entered the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, Maozhen led a great army against Zhu Quanzhong, was beaten, and returned at dusk with Bian troops in pursuit almost through the west gate.

sentences.zh: 己亥，再起復前戶部侍郎、同平章事韋貽范，使姚洎草制。

translations.literal: On jihai day, former Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Minister Wei Yifan was again recalled from mourning; Yao Ji was made to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, former vice minister of revenue and associate chief minister Wei Yifan was recalled from mourning again, with Yao Ji ordered to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 貽范不讓，即表謝，明日，視事。

translations.literal: Yifan did not decline and at once submitted a memorial of thanks; the next day he took up office.
translations.idiomatic: Yifan did not decline, submitted his thanks at once, and took up office the next day.

sentences.zh: 西川兵請假道於興元，山南西道節度使李繼密遣兵戍三泉以拒之。

translations.literal: Xichuan troops requested passage through Xingyuan; Shannan West Circuit military governor Li Jimi sent troops to garrison Sanquan to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan forces asked passage through Xingyuan; Shannan West Circuit military governor Li Jimi garrisoned Sanquan to block them.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，西川前鋒將王宗播攻之，不克，退保山寨。

translations.literal: On xinchou day, the Xichuan vanguard general Wang Zongbo attacked them but could not overcome them and withdrew to hold a mountain stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day, Xichuan vanguard Wang Zongbo attacked but failed and withdrew to a mountain stockade.

sentences.zh: 親吏柳修業謂宗播曰：「公舉族歸人，不為之死戰，何以自保？」

translations.literal: His personal clerk Liu Xiuye said to Zongbo: "My lord brought your whole clan to submit to another—if you do not fight to the death for him, how can you preserve yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: His personal clerk Liu Xiuye said to Zongbo, "You brought your whole clan to submit—if you will not fight to the death for your lord, how will you save yourselves?

sentences.zh: 宗播令其眾曰：「吾與汝曹決戰取功名；

translations.literal: Zongbo ordered his multitude: "I will fight a decisive battle with you to win merit and fame;
translations.idiomatic: Zongbo told his men, "I will fight a decisive battle with you for honor and reward;

sentences.zh: 不爾，死於此！」

translations.literal: otherwise, die here!"
translations.idiomatic: otherwise we die here!"

sentences.zh: 遂破金牛、黑水、西縣、褒城四寨。

translations.literal: They then broke the four stockades of Jinniu, Heishui, Xixian, and Baocheng.
translations.idiomatic: They then captured the four stockades at Jinniu, Heishui, Xixian, and Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 軍校秦承厚攻西縣，矢貫左目，達於右目，鏃不出。

translations.literal: The army officer Qin Chenghou attacked Xixian; an arrow pierced his left eye and reached his right eye, and the arrowhead would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Army officer Qin Chenghou led the assault on Xixian and took an arrow through his left eye and out his right; the head could not be removed.

sentences.zh: 王建自舐其創，膿潰鏃出。

translations.literal: Wang Jian himself licked his wound; when the pus broke, the arrowhead came out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian licked the wound himself; when the pus burst, the arrowhead came free.

sentences.zh: 王宗播攻馬盤寨，繼密戰敗，奔還漢中。

translations.literal: Wang Zongbo attacked Mapan stockade; Jimi was defeated in battle and fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbo attacked Mapan stockade; Jimi was beaten and fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 西川軍乘勝至城下，王宗滌帥眾先登，遂克之，繼密請降，遷於成都。

translations.literal: The Xichuan army pressed the victory to the foot of the city wall; Wang Zongdi led the multitude in the first ascent, then took it; Jimi requested surrender and was moved to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan forces pressed their advantage to the walls; Wang Zongdi led the first assault and took the city. Jimi surrendered and was sent to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 得兵三萬，騎五千，宗滌入屯漢中。

translations.literal: They obtained thirty thousand infantry and five thousand cavalry; Zongdi entered and encamped at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They took thirty thousand troops and five thousand horses, and Zongdi garrisoned Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 王建曰：「繼密殘賊三輔，以其降，不忍殺。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian said: "Jimi ravaged the Three Adjuncts as a remnant rebel; because he surrendered, I cannot bear to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian said, "Jimi ravaged the Three Adjuncts as a rebel holdout; since he has surrendered, I cannot bring myself to kill him.

sentences.zh: 復其姓名曰王萬弘，不時召見諸將陵易之。

translations.literal: He restored his original name to Wang Wanhong and from time to time summoned him before the generals, who treated him with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He restored his original name, Wang Wanhong, and from time to time had him appear before the generals, who humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 萬弘終日縱酒，俳優輩亦加戲誚。

translations.literal: Wanhong drank all day long, and the actors also added mockery and ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Wanhong drank all day, and the entertainers piled on taunts and ridicule.

sentences.zh: 萬弘不勝憂憤，醉投池水而卒。

translations.literal: Wanhong could not bear grief and anger; drunk, he threw himself into a pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the shame and rage, Wanhong got drunk, threw himself into a pool, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 詔以王宗滌為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wang Zongdi military governor of the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Wang Zongdi military governor of the Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗滌有勇略，得眾心，王建忌之。

translations.literal: Zongdi had courage and strategy and won the hearts of the multitude; Wang Jian was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdi was bold and capable and won the troops' loyalty, and Wang Jian grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 建作府門，繪以朱丹，蜀人謂之「畫紅樓」，建以宗滌姓名應之，王宗佶等疾其功，復構以飛語。

translations.literal: Jian built a prefectural gate and painted it with cinnabar; the people of Shu called it the "Cinnabar-painted Tower," and Jian took Zongdi's name as corresponding to it; Wang Zongji and others resented his merit and again fabricated slanderous rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Jian built a new prefectural gate and painted it red; the people of Shu called it the "Scarlet Tower," and Jian claimed Zongdi's name matched the omen. Wang Zongji and others, envious of his achievements, spread fresh rumors against him.

sentences.zh: 建召宗滌至成都，詰責之，宗滌曰：「三蜀略平，大王聽讒，殺功臣可矣。」

translations.literal: Jian summoned Zongdi to Chengdu and interrogated and rebuked him; Zongdi said: "The Three Shu are nearly pacified; if the great king listens to slander, you may as well kill your meritorious minister."
translations.idiomatic: Jian summoned Zongdi to Chengdu and rebuked him. Zongdi said, "The Three Shu are nearly pacified; if you listen to slander, go ahead and kill your loyal general.

sentences.zh: 建命親隨馬軍都指揮使唐道襲夜飲之酒，縊殺之，成都為之罷市，連營涕泣，如喪親戚。

translations.literal: Jian ordered his personal attendant, cavalry commander Tang Daoxi, to give him wine at night and then strangle him to death; Chengdu closed its markets for him, and camp after camp wept as if mourning kin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had his personal attendant and cavalry commander Tang Daoxi ply him with wine at night and then strangle him. Chengdu shut its markets in mourning, and camp after camp wept as though they had lost kin.

sentences.zh: 建以指揮使王宗賀權興元留後。

translations.literal: Jian made the commander Wang Zonghe acting regent of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian appointed commander Wang Zonghe acting regent of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 道襲，閬州人也，始以舞童事建，後浸預謀畫。

translations.literal: Daoxi was a man of Langzhou; he first served Jian as a dancing boy and later gradually came to take part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi was from Langzhou. He had begun as a dancing boy in Jian's service and gradually came to share in his counsels.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳，朱全忠以久雨，士卒病，召諸將議引兵歸河中，親從指揮使高季昌、左開道指揮使劉知俊曰：「天下英雄，窺此舉一歲矣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yisi day, Zhu Quanzhong, because of long rains and sick soldiers, summoned the generals to discuss withdrawing the army to Hezhong; his personal attendant commander Gao Jichang and Left Vanguard commander Liu Zhijun said: "The heroes of the realm have watched this campaign for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi day, prolonged rain had sickened Zhu Quanzhong's troops, and he called his generals to discuss pulling back to Hezhong. His personal attendant commander Gao Jichang and Left Vanguard commander Liu Zhijun said, "Every power in the realm has watched this siege for a year.

sentences.zh: 今茂貞已困，奈何捨之去！」

translations.literal: Now Maozhen is already cornered—how can we abandon him and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen is already at bay—how can we walk away now!

sentences.zh: 全忠患李茂貞堅壁不出，季昌請以譎計誘致之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was troubled that Li Maozhen held his walls and would not come out; Jichang requested using a stratagem to lure him out.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was frustrated that Li Maozhen would not leave his walls, and Jichang proposed a ruse to draw him out.

sentences.zh: 募有能入城為諜者，騎士馬景請行，曰：「此行必死，願大王錄其妻子。」

translations.literal: He recruited anyone who could enter the city as a spy; the cavalryman Ma Jing volunteered, saying: "This mission will surely mean death; I ask the great king to provide for my wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: He sought someone who could enter the city as a spy. Cavalryman Ma Jing stepped forward and said, "This mission will cost me my life; I ask that you provide for my wife and children.

sentences.zh: 全忠惻然止之，景不可。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was moved and tried to stop him, but Jing would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was moved and tried to dissuade him, but Jing would not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 時全忠遣朱友倫發兵於大梁，明日將至，當出兵迓之。

translations.literal: At that time Quanzhong had sent Zhu Youlun to raise troops at Daliang; they would arrive the next day, and troops should go out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had already sent Zhu Youlun to raise troops at Daliang; they were due the next day, and the army would have to march out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 景請因此時給駿馬雜眾騎而出，全忠從之，命諸軍皆秣馬飽士。

translations.literal: Jing asked that at this time he be given a fine horse and go out mixed among the multitude of riders; Quanzhong agreed and ordered all the armies to feed their horses and fill their men.
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked to take a swift horse and ride out among the other horsemen at that moment. Quanzhong agreed and ordered every unit to feed its horses and fill its men's bellies.

sentences.zh: 丁未旦，偃旗幟潛伏，無得妄出，營中寂如無人。

translations.literal: At dawn on dingwei day, flags and banners were lowered and the army lay hidden; no one was to go out without cause, and the camp was silent as if empty.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on dingwei day the army lowered its banners and lay hidden; no one was to stir without orders, and the camp fell silent as if deserted.

sentences.zh: 景與眾騎皆出，忽躍馬西去，詐為逃亡，入城告茂貞曰：「全忠舉軍遁矣，獨留傷病者近萬人守營，今夕亦去矣，請速擊之！」

translations.literal: Jing went out with the multitude of riders, then suddenly spurred his horse westward, feigning flight; entering the city he told Maozhen: "Quanzhong has fled with the whole army, leaving only nearly ten thousand wounded and sick to hold the camp; tonight they too will leave—please strike quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing rode out with the other horsemen, then suddenly spurred west as if deserting. Inside the city he told Maozhen, "Quanzhong has fled with the whole army, leaving nearly ten thousand wounded and sick to hold the camp; they will pull out tonight too—strike at once!

sentences.zh: 於是茂貞開門，悉眾攻全忠營，全忠鼓於中軍，百營俱出，縱兵擊之，又遣數百騎據其城門，鳳翔軍進退失據，自蹈藉，殺傷殆盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Maozhen opened the gates and sent out his whole force to attack Quanzhong's camp; Quanzhong beat the drums in the central army, a hundred camps all came out, and he unleashed his troops to strike them; he also sent several hundred riders to seize their city gates; the Fengxiang army lost footing whether advancing or retreating, trampled one another, and were nearly all killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen opened the gates and sent his whole force against Quanzhong's camp. Quanzhong sounded the drums at headquarters, every camp poured out, and he sent hundreds of riders to seize the gates. The Fengxiang army lost all room to advance or retreat, trampled one another, and was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 茂貞自是喪氣，始議與全忠連和，奉車駕還京，不復以詔書勒全忠還鎮矣。

translations.literal: From this Maozhen lost his fighting spirit and first discussed making peace with Quanzhong, escorting the imperial carriage back to the capital, and no longer using edicts to compel Quanzhong to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Maozhen lost heart and began to talk peace with Quanzhong, offering to send the emperor back to the capital and no longer pressing him with edicts to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 全忠表季昌為宋州團練使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized to appoint Jichang regimental commissioner of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong recommended Jichang for appointment as regimental commissioner of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 季昌，硤石人，本朱友恭之僕夫也。

translations.literal: Jichang was a man of Xiashi and had originally been a servant of Zhu Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang was from Xiashi and had once been a servant of Zhu Yougong.

sentences.zh: 戊申，武定節度使李思敬以洋州降王建。

translations.literal: On wushen day, Wuding military governor Li Sijing surrendered Yangzhou to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day, Wuding military governor Li Sijing surrendered Yangzhou to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，李茂貞盡出騎兵於鄰州就芻糧。

translations.literal: On xinhai day, Li Maozhen sent out all his cavalry to neighboring prefectures to obtain fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day, Li Maozhen sent all his cavalry into neighboring prefectures to forage for fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 壬子，朱全忠穿蚰蜒壕圍鳳翔，設大舖、鈴架以絕內外。

translations.literal: On renzi day, Zhu Quanzhong dug winding trenches to surround Fengxiang and set up large sheds and bell frames to cut off inside from outside.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, Zhu Quanzhong dug serpentine trenches around Fengxiang and erected large sheds and alarm frames to seal the city off.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以茂貞為鳳翔、靜難、武定、昭武四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: On guihai day, Maozhen was made military governor of the four commands of Fengxiang, Jingnan, Wuding, and Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day, Maozhen was confirmed as military governor of Fengxiang, Jingnan, Wuding, and Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 或勸錢鏐渡江東保越州，以避徐、許之難。

translations.literal: Some advised Qian Liu to cross the river east and hold Yuezhou to avoid the trouble from Xu Kuan and Xu Zaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Qian Liu to cross the river to Yuezhou and make a stand there to escape the threat from Xu Kuan and Xu Zaisi.

sentences.zh: 杜建微按劍叱之曰：「事或不濟，同死於此，豈可復東度乎！」

translations.literal: Du Jianhui grasped his sword and shouted at them: "If matters do not succeed, we die here together—how can we cross east again!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Jianhui drew his sword and shouted them down: "If we fail, we die here together—how can we flee east again!

sentences.zh: 鏐恐徐綰等據越州，遣大將顧全武將兵戍之。

translations.literal: Liu feared that Xu Kuan and the others would seize Yuezhou and sent the great general Gu Quanwu to lead troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu feared Xu Kuan might seize Yuezhou and sent his chief general Gu Quanwu to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 全武曰：「越州不足往，不若之廣陵。

translations.literal: Quanwu said: "Yuezhou is not worth going to; better to go to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu said, "Yuezhou is no refuge—we should go to Guangling instead.

sentences.zh: 鏐曰：「何故？」

translations.literal: Liu said: "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu asked, "Why?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聞綰等謀詔田頵，田頵至，淮南助之，不可敵也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I hear Kuan and the others plan to summon Tian Yun; when Yun arrives, Huainan will aid them, and we cannot be matched."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I hear Kuan and his allies mean to summon Tian Yun. Once Yun arrives with Huainan's backing, we cannot stand against them.

sentences.zh: 建徽曰：「孫儒之難，王嘗有德於楊公，今往告之，宜有以相報。」

translations.literal: Jianhui said: "In Sun Ru's crisis, the king once did a kindness for Lord Yang; if we go now to tell him, he ought to repay it in some way."
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui said, "When Sun Ru threatened us, you once did Yang a favor. If we appeal to him now, he should repay it.

sentences.zh: 鏐命全武告急於楊行密，全武曰：「徒往無益，請得王子為質。」

translations.literal: Liu ordered Quanwu to report the emergency to Yang Xingmi; Quanwu said: "Going empty-handed will do no good—I ask to take a princely son as hostage."
translations.idiomatic: Liu ordered Quanwu to seek aid from Yang Xingmi. Quanwu said, "A bare appeal will do no good—I need a prince as hostage.

sentences.zh: 鏐命其子傳鐐微服為全武僕，與偕之廣陵，且求婚於行密。

translations.literal: Liu ordered his son Chuanliao to dress in plain clothes as Quanwu's servant and go with him to Guangling, and also to request a marriage alliance with Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu sent his son Chuanliao in plain dress as Quanwu's servant to Guangling and asked for a marriage alliance with Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 過潤州，團練使安仁義愛傅鐐清麗，將以十僕易之。

translations.literal: Passing Runzhou, the regimental commissioner An Renyi took a liking to Chuanliao's refined beauty and intended to exchange ten servants for him.
translations.idiomatic: At Runzhou, regimental commissioner An Renyi was taken with Chuanliao's handsome looks and tried to trade ten servants for him.

sentences.zh: 全武夜半賂閽者逃去。

translations.literal: Quanwu bribed the gatekeepers at midnight and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu bribed the gatekeepers at midnight and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 綰等果召田頵，頵引兵赴之，先遣親吏何饒謂鏐曰：「請大王東如越州，空府廨以相待，無為殺士卒！」
