translations.literal: Kuan and the others indeed summoned Tian Yun; Yun led troops to join them and first sent his personal clerk He Rao to tell Liu: "I ask the great king to go east to Yuezhou and leave the government offices empty to await us—do not kill soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: Kuan and his allies did summon Tian Yun, who marched to join them and first sent his clerk He Rao to Liu with this message: "Go east to Yuezhou and leave your offices empty for us—spare your soldiers' lives!

sentences.zh: 鏐報曰：「軍中叛亂，何方無之！

translations.literal: Liu replied: "Mutiny in the army—where is there none!
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "Mutiny happens in every army!

sentences.zh: 公為節帥，乃助賊為逆。

translations.literal: You are a military governor, yet you aid rebels in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a governor's commission, yet you aid rebels in treason.

sentences.zh: 戰則亟戰，又何大言！」

translations.literal: If you wish to fight, then fight quickly—why such big talk!"
translations.idiomatic: If you want a fight, then fight—enough of your bluster!

sentences.zh: 頵築壘絕往來之道。

translations.literal: Yun built stockades to cut off the routes of travel.
translations.idiomatic: Yun threw up fortifications and cut off the roads.

sentences.zh: 鏐患之，募能奪其地者賞以州。

translations.literal: Liu was troubled by this and offered a prefecture as reward to anyone who could seize the position back.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Liu offered a prefecture to whoever could break the blockade.

sentences.zh: 衢州制置使陳璋將卒三百出城奮擊，遂奪其地，鏐即以為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Quzhou system-making commissioner Chen Zhang led three hundred soldiers out of the city in a fierce attack, then recovered the position; Liu at once made him prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou commissioner Chen Zhang led three hundred men out in a fierce assault, broke the blockade, and Liu immediately made him prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 顧全武至廣陵，說楊行密曰：「使田頵得志，必為王患。

translations.literal: Gu Quanwu reached Guangling and urged Yang Xingmi: "If Tian Yun gets his way, he will surely become a calamity for the king.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu reached Guangling and told Yang Xingmi, "If Tian Yun succeeds, he will become your gravest threat.

sentences.zh: 王召頵還，錢王請以子傳□□為質，且求婚。」

translations.literal: If the king recalls Yun, the King of Qian asks to leave his son Chuanliao as hostage and also requests a marriage alliance."
translations.idiomatic: Recall Yun, and the King of Qian will leave his son Chuanliao as hostage and seek a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 行密許之，以女妻傅鐐。

translations.literal: Xingmi agreed and gave his daughter in marriage to Chuanliao.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi agreed and gave his daughter to Chuanliao in marriage.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，李儼至楊州，楊行密始建制敕院，每有封拜，輒以告儼，於紫極宮玄宗像前陳制書，再拜然後下。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Li Yan arrived at Yangzhou; Yang Xingmi then established an edict-proclamation office, and whenever there was an appointment or enfeoffment he would inform Yan, present the edict before the image of Emperor Xuanzong in Ziji Palace, bow twice, and only then descend.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Li Yan arrived at Yangzhou. Yang Xingmi then set up an office for imperial edicts; whenever he made an appointment or enfeoffment, he informed Yan, presented the edict before the image of Emperor Xuanzong in Ziji Palace, bowed twice, and only then took his seat.

sentences.zh: 王建攻拔興州，以軍使王宗浩為興州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Jian attacked and took Xingzhou and made army commissioner Wang Zonghao prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian captured Xingzhou and appointed army commissioner Wang Zonghao its prefect.

sentences.zh: 戊寅夜，李茂貞假子彥詢帥三團步兵奔於汴軍。

translations.literal: On the night of wuyin day, Li Maozhen's adopted son Yanxun led three regiments of infantry in flight to the Bian army.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wuyin day, Li Maozhen's adopted son Yanxun led three infantry regiments in desertion to the Bian camp.

sentences.zh: 己卯，李彥韜繼之。

translations.literal: On jimao day, Li Yantao followed after him.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day, Li Yantao followed suit.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，朱全忠遣幕僚司馬鄴奉表入城。

translations.literal: On gengchen day, Zhu Quanzhong sent his staff member Sima Ye to present a memorial and enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day, Zhu Quanzhong sent staff officer Sima Ye into the city with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 甲申，又遣使獻熊白，自是獻食物、繒帛相繼。

translations.literal: On jiashen day, he again sent envoys to present bear's paw; from then on gifts of food and silk followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day he sent envoys again, this time with bear's paw, and thereafter food and silk gifts arrived in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 上皆先以示李茂貞，使啟視之，茂貞亦不敢啟。

translations.literal: The emperor always showed them first to Li Maozhen and had him open and look; Maozhen also did not dare to open them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always showed the gifts to Li Maozhen first and had him open them, but Maozhen did not dare.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，復遣使請與茂貞議連和，民出城樵采者皆不抄掠。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, he again sent envoys requesting to discuss peace with Maozhen, and civilians who went out of the city to gather firewood were not plundered.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day he sent envoys again to negotiate peace with Maozhen, and civilians who left the city to gather firewood were left unmolested.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，全忠表請修宮闕及迎車駕。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Quanzhong memorialized requesting repair of the palace halls and escorting the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Quanzhong memorialized asking to restore the palace and escort the emperor home.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遣國子司業薛昌祚、內使王延繢繼詔賜全忠。

translations.literal: On jichou day, he sent Director of the Directorate of Education Xue Changzuo and palace commissioner Wang Yanhui with successive edicts bestowed on Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he sent Directorate of Education director Xue Changzuo and palace commissioner Wang Yanhui with further edicts for Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，茂貞復出兵擊汴軍城西寨，敗還。

translations.literal: On guisi day, Maozhen again sent troops out to attack the Bian army's west-camp stockade and returned defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Maozhen attacked the Bian camp west of the city again and was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 全忠以絳袍衣降者，使招呼城中人，鳳翔軍夜縋去，及因樵采去不返者甚眾。

translations.literal: Quanzhong clothed defectors in crimson robes and had them summon the people in the city; by night Fengxiang troops were lowered on ropes and fled, and very many also left on pretext of gathering firewood and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong dressed defectors in crimson robes and had them call to the city. Fengxiang troops slipped out by rope at night, and many others left on the pretext of gathering firewood and never came back.

sentences.zh: 是後茂貞或遣兵出擊汴軍，多不為用，散還。

translations.literal: After this, when Maozhen sometimes sent troops out to strike the Bian army, many would not obey and dispersed back.
translations.idiomatic: After that, when Maozhen sent troops out against the Bian army, many refused to fight and drifted back.

sentences.zh: 茂貞疑上與全忠有密約，壬寅，更於御院北垣外增兵防衛。

translations.literal: Maozhen suspected the emperor had a secret pact with Quanzhong; on renyin day he added more troops for defense outside the north wall of the imperial compound.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting a secret pact between the emperor and Quanzhong, Maozhen on renyin day posted more guards outside the north wall of the imperial compound.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸卯朔，保大節度使李茂勳帥其眾萬餘人救鳳翔，屯於城北阪上，與城中舉烽相應。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the guimao new moon, Baoda military governor Li Maoxun led his multitude of more than ten thousand to rescue Fengxiang, encamped on the slope north of the city, and raised beacon fires in response with those inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the guimao new moon, Baoda military governor Li Maoxun marched more than ten thousand men to relieve Fengxiang, camped on the slope north of the city, and exchanged beacon signals with the defenders.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上使趙國夫人詗學士院二使皆不在，亟召韓偓、姚洎，竊見之於土門外，執手相泣。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, the emperor sent the Lady of Zhao to inquire at the Academy; the two commissioners were both absent, and he urgently summoned Han Wo and Yao Ji and secretly met them outside Tumen Gate, grasping hands and weeping together.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day the emperor sent the Lady of Zhao to the Hanlin Academy, but both commissioners were away. He urgently summoned Han Wo and Yao Ji and met them secretly outside Tumen Gate, weeping as they clasped hands.

sentences.zh: 洎請上速還，恐為它人所見，上遽去。

translations.literal: Ji asked the emperor to return quickly, fearing others would see; the emperor hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ji urged the emperor to return at once, fearing they would be seen, and the emperor hurried off.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣其將孔勍、李暉將兵乘虛襲鄜、坊。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent his generals Kong Qing and Li Hui to lead troops and seize the opportunity to raid Yan and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Kong Qing and Li Hui to strike Yan and Fang while their defenses were thin.

sentences.zh: 壬子，拔坊州。

translations.literal: On renzi day, they took Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day they captured Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大雪，汴軍冒之夕進，五鼓，抵庸阜州城下。

translations.literal: On jiayin day, heavy snow fell; the Bian army braved it and advanced by night; at the fifth watch they reached the foot of Yongfu prefecture's walls.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day a heavy snow fell. The Bian army marched through it by night and at the fifth watch reached the walls of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄜人不為備，汴軍入城，城中兵尚八千人，格鬥至午，鄜人始敗，擒留守李繼鐐。

translations.literal: The people of Yan were unprepared; the Bian army entered the city; the troops in the city still numbered eight thousand; they fought hand to hand until noon before the people of Yan were defeated; they captured the regent Li Jiliao.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yanzhou were unprepared. The Bian army entered the city, where eight thousand defenders fought until noon before yielding. They captured regent Li Jiliao.

sentences.zh: 就撫存李茂勳及將士之家，按堵無擾，命李暉權知軍府事。

translations.literal: They then comforted and preserved the households of Li Maoxun and the officers and soldiers, keeping order without disturbance, and appointed Li Hui acting commander of the military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They reassured the families of Maoxun and his officers, kept the city quiet, and put Li Hui in temporary charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 茂勳聞之，引兵遁去。

translations.literal: When Maoxun heard of it, he led his troops and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoxun heard the news, he fled with his army.

sentences.zh: 汴軍每夜鳴鼓角，城中地如動。

translations.literal: Each night the Bian army sounded drums and horns, and the ground in the city seemed to shake.
translations.idiomatic: Each night the Bian drums and horns shook the ground inside the city.

sentences.zh: 攻城者詬城上人云「劫天子賊」，乘城者詬城下人云「奪天子賊」。

translations.literal: Those attacking the city cursed those atop the walls, calling them "bandits who kidnapped the Son of Heaven"; those manning the walls cursed those below, calling them "bandits who seize the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers shouted at the walls, "Kidnappers of the emperor!" The defenders shouted back, "Usurpers of the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 是冬，大雪，城中食盡，凍餒死者不可勝計，或臥未死，肉已為人所冎。

translations.literal: That winter, heavy snow fell; food in the city was exhausted, and those who died of cold and hunger were beyond counting; some lay not yet dead while their flesh was already cut up by others.
translations.idiomatic: That winter snow piled deep, food ran out, and the dead from cold and hunger were beyond count. Some still lay alive while others butchered them for meat.

sentences.zh: 市中賣人肉斤直錢百，犬肉值五百。

translations.literal: In the market human flesh sold for a hundred cash per jin, and dog meat fetched five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Human flesh sold in the market for a hundred cash a pound; dog meat went for five hundred.

sentences.zh: 茂貞儲偫亦竭，以犬彘供御膳。

translations.literal: Maozhen's stored provisions were also exhausted, and dogs and swine were used for the imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen's stores were gone too, and the imperial table was fed on dog and pig.

sentences.zh: 上鬻御衣及小皇子衣於市以充用，削漬松梯以飼御馬。

translations.literal: The emperor sold imperial robes and the young princes' clothes in the market to meet expenses, and shaved soaked pine ladders to feed the imperial horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sold imperial robes and the young princes' clothes in the market to raise money, and shaved soaked pine ladders to feed the imperial horses.

sentences.zh: 丙子，戶部侍郎、同平章事韋貽范薨。

translations.literal: On bingzi day, Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Minister Wei Yifan died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, vice minister of revenue and associate chief minister Wei Yifan died.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，朱全忠遣人薙城外草以困城中。

translations.literal: On guihai day, Zhu Quanzhong sent men to mow the grass outside the city walls to distress those inside.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Zhu Quanzhong had the grass outside the walls cut to deny the city any forage.

sentences.zh: 甲子，李茂貞增兵守宮門，諸宦官自度不免，互相尤怨。

translations.literal: On jiazi day, Li Maozhen added troops to guard the palace gates; the eunuchs, each judging himself beyond escape, blamed and resented one another.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Maozhen posted more guards at the palace gates. The eunuchs, each sure he would not survive, turned on one another in blame and recrimination.

sentences.zh: 蘇檢數為韓偓經營入相，言於茂貞及中尉、樞密，且遣親吏告偓，偓怒曰：「公與韋公自貶所召歸，旬月致位宰相，訖不能有所為。

translations.literal: Su Jian repeatedly worked to maneuver Han Wo into the chancellorship, speaking to Maozhen and the chief eunuchs and Privy Council officials, and also sent a personal clerk to tell Wo; Wo angrily said: "You and Lord Wei were recalled from exile and within ten days and a month reached the rank of chief minister, yet in the end could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jian had been lobbying to make Han Wo chief minister, speaking to Maozhen and the chief eunuchs and also sending a personal clerk to tell Wo. Wo snapped, "You and Wei Yifan were recalled from exile and made chief ministers within a month, yet you accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 今朝夕不濟，乃欲以此相污邪！」

translations.literal: Now, with morning and evening unsettled, you would use this to stain me as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Now, with the court on the brink of ruin, you would drag me down with you!

sentences.zh: 田頵急攻杭州，仍具舟將自西陵渡江。

translations.literal: Tian Yun pressed the attack on Hangzhou and also prepared boats intending to cross the river himself from Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun pressed the attack on Hangzhou and prepared boats to cross the river from Xiling himself.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐遣其將盛造、朱郁拒破之。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent his generals Sheng Zao and Zhu Yu to resist and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Sheng Zao and Zhu Yu to repel and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李茂勳遣使請降於朱全忠，更名周彝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Maoxun sent envoys requesting surrender to Zhu Quanzhong and changed his name to Zhou Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Maoxun sent envoys to surrender to Zhu Quanzhong and changed his name to Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 於是茂貞山南州鎮皆入王建，關中州鎮皆入全忠，坐守孤城。

translations.literal: Thereupon Maozhen's prefectures and commands south of the mountains all passed to Wang Jian, and the prefectures and commands of Guanzhong all passed to Quanzhong; he sat guarding an isolated city.
translations.idiomatic: By then every prefecture south of the mountains had fallen to Wang Jian and every stronghold in Guanzhong to Quanzhong, leaving Maozhen holding a lone city.

sentences.zh: 乃密謀誅宦官以自贖，遺全忠書曰：「禍亂之興，皆由全誨。

translations.literal: He then secretly plotted to execute the eunuchs to redeem himself and sent Quanzhong a letter saying: "The rise of calamity and disorder all comes from Han Quanhui.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly plotted to kill the eunuchs to redeem himself and wrote Quanzhong: "This disaster began with Han Quanhui.

sentences.zh: 僕迎駕至此，以備他盜。

translations.literal: Your servant welcomed the imperial carriage here to guard against other robbers.
translations.idiomatic: I brought the emperor here to protect him from other predators.

sentences.zh: 公既志匡社稷，請公迎扈還宮，僕以弊甲雕兵，從公陳力。」

translations.literal: Since the lord's will is to restore the state altars, I ask the lord to welcome and escort the emperor back to the palace; your servant with worn armor and depleted troops will follow the lord and exert his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Since you mean to restore the realm, welcome the emperor back to the capital and I will follow with what battered troops I have left.

sentences.zh: 全忠復書曰：「僕舉兵至此，正以乘輿播遷；

translations.literal: Quanzhong replied in a letter: "Your servant raised troops and came here precisely because the imperial carriage was driven into exile;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wrote back: "I marched here because the emperor was driven from the capital;

sentences.zh: 公能協力，固所願也。」

translations.literal: if the lord can cooperate in strength, that is indeed what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: if you will work with me, that is exactly what I want."

sentences.zh: 楊行密使人召田頵曰：「不還，吾且使人代鎮宣州。」

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent someone to summon Tian Yun, saying: "If you do not return, I shall send someone to replace you as commander of Xuanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent for Tian Yun with this message: "If you do not return, I will replace you as governor of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，頵將還，征犒軍錢二十萬緡於錢鏐，且求鏐子為質，將妻以女。

translations.literal: On gengchen day, as Yun was about to return, he levied two hundred thousand strings in reward money for the troops from Qian Liu, and also demanded one of Liu's sons as a hostage, giving his wife in marriage to a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day, as Yun prepared to withdraw, he exacted two hundred thousand strings in troop-reward money from Qian Liu, demanded a son of Liu as hostage, and offered his own wife's hand to a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 鏐謂諸子：「孰能為田氏婿者？」

translations.literal: Liu said to his sons: "Who can become the Tian clan's son-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu asked his sons, "Which of you will marry into the Tian family?

sentences.zh: 莫對。

translations.literal: No one answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one replied.

sentences.zh: 鏐欲遣幼子傳球，傳球不可。

translations.literal: Liu wanted to send his youngest son Chuanqiu; Chuanqiu refused.
translations.idiomatic: Liu meant to send his youngest son Chuanqiu, but Chuanqiu would not go.

sentences.zh: 鏐怒，將殺之。

translations.literal: Liu grew angry and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Liu was on the point of executing him.

sentences.zh: 次子傳瓘請行，吳夫人泣曰：「奈何置兒虎口！」

translations.literal: The second son Chuangun volunteered to go; Lady Wu wept and said: "How can you send a child into the tiger's maw!"
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Chuangun, offered to go instead. Lady Wu wept and cried, "How can you throw our son to the tiger!

sentences.zh: 傳鏐曰：「紓國家之難，安敢愛身！」

translations.literal: Chuangun said: "To ease the state's distress—how would I dare spare my own life!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuangun replied, "To relieve the realm's peril—how could I cling to my own life!

sentences.zh: 再拜而出，鏐泣送之。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and went out; Liu wept as he saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and departed; Liu wept as he sent him away.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘從數人縋北門而下。

translations.literal: Chuangun, with a few men, was lowered by rope from the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuangun and a handful of men were let down by rope from the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 頵與徐綰、許再思同歸宣州。

translations.literal: Yun returned to Xuanzhou together with Xu Wan and Xu Zaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun withdrew to Xuanzhou with Xu Wan and Xu Zaisi.

sentences.zh: 鏐奪傳球內牙兵印。

translations.literal: Liu seized Chuanqiu's seal of the Inner Guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu stripped Chuanqiu of his seal as commander of the Inner Guard.

sentences.zh: 越州客軍指揮使張洪以徐綰之黨自疑，帥步兵三百奔衢州，刺史陳璋納之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hong, commander of the guest army at Yuezhou, suspecting himself among Xu Wan's faction, led three hundred foot soldiers in flight to Quzhou; Prefect Chen Zhang accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong, commander of the Yuezhou guest army, fearing guilt by association with Xu Wan's party, led three hundred foot soldiers in flight to Quzhou, where Prefect Chen Zhang took them in.

sentences.zh: 溫州將丁章逐刺史朱敖，敖奔福州。

translations.literal: The Wenzhou general Ding Zhang drove out Prefect Zhu Ao; Ao fled to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Zhang, a Wenzhou officer, expelled Prefect Zhu Ao, who fled to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 章據溫州，田頵遣使招之，道出衢州。

translations.literal: Zhang held Wenzhou; Tian Yun sent envoys to recruit him, and the route passed through Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang seized Wenzhou. Tian Yun sent envoys to win him over, and their route lay through Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳璋聽其往還，錢鏐由是恨璋。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang allowed them to come and go; Qian Liu therefore came to hate Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang let the envoys pass freely in both directions, and Qian Liu came to resent him for it.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上召李茂貞、蘇檢、李繼誨、李彥弼、李繼岌、李繼遠、李繼忠食，議與朱全忠和，上曰：「十六宅諸王以下，凍餒死者日有數人。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, the emperor summoned Li Maozhen, Su Jian, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, Li Jiji, Li Jiyuan, and Li Jizhong to a meal and discussed peace with Zhu Quanzhong. The emperor said: "Among the princes of the Sixteen Mansions and below, several people freeze or starve to death each day.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the emperor summoned Li Maozhen, Su Jian, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, Li Jiji, Li Jiyuan, and Li Jizhong to dine and discuss peace with Zhu Quanzhong. The emperor said, "Below the princes of the Sixteen Mansions, several people die of cold and hunger every day.

sentences.zh: 在內諸王及公主、妃嬪，一日食粥，一日食湯餅，今亦竭矣。

translations.literal: The princes inside the palace, princesses, and consorts eat gruel one day and soup-noodles the next—and even that is now exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The princes within the palace, the princesses, and the consorts alternate gruel one day with soup-noodles the next—and even that is gone.

sentences.zh: 卿等意如何？」

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you counsel?"

sentences.zh: 皆不對。

translations.literal: None answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one spoke.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「速當和解耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We must make peace quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We must settle this at once!"

sentences.zh: 鳳翔兵十餘人遮韓全誨於左銀台門，喧罵曰：「闔境塗炭，闔城餒死，正為軍容輩數人耳！」

translations.literal: More than ten Fengxiang soldiers blocked Han Quanhui at the Left Yintai Gate, shouting abuse: "The whole region is scorched, the whole city starves— and all for the sake of a few Military Affairs Commissioners like you!"
translations.idiomatic: A dozen Fengxiang soldiers waylaid Han Quanhui at the Left Yintai Gate and shouted, "The whole country burns, the whole city starves—and for what? For a handful of Military Affairs Commissioners like you!

sentences.zh: 全誨叩頭訴於茂貞，茂貞曰：「卒輩何知！」

translations.literal: Quanhui kowtowed and appealed to Maozhen; Maozhen said: "What do common soldiers know!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui kowtowed and pleaded with Maozhen, who said, "What do rank-and-file soldiers know!

sentences.zh: 命酌酒兩杯，對飲而罷。

translations.literal: He ordered two cups of wine poured; they drank facing each other and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: He had two cups of wine poured; they drank together and let it drop.

sentences.zh: 又訴於上，上亦諭解之。

translations.literal: Quanhui appealed again to the emperor, and the emperor also instructed them to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui appealed to the emperor as well, and the emperor too urged reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 李繼昭謂全誨曰：「昔楊軍容破楊守亮一族，今軍容亦破繼昭一族邪！」

translations.literal: Li Jizhao said to Quanhui: "In the past Military Affairs Commissioner Yang destroyed the whole clan of Yang Shouliang—will Military Affairs Commissioner now destroy Jizhao's whole clan as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhao told Quanhui, "Yang the Military Affairs Commissioner once wiped out Yang Shouliang's entire clan—is this Military Affairs Commissioner going to wipe out Jizhao's clan too!

sentences.zh: 慢罵之，遂出降於全忠，複姓苻，名道昭。

translations.literal: He reviled Quanhui contemptuously, then went out and surrendered to Quanzhong, restoring his original surname Fu and taking the name Daozhao.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed Quanhui to his face, then left and surrendered to Quanzhong, resuming his original surname Fu and the name Daozhao.

sentences.zh: 是歲，虔州刺史盧光稠攻嶺南，陷韶州，使其子延昌守之，進圍潮州。

translations.literal: That year, Lu Guangchou, prefect of Qianzhou, attacked Lingnan, captured Shaozhou, and set his son Yanchang to hold it, then advanced to besiege Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lu Guangchou, prefect of Qianzhou, attacked Lingnan, took Shaozhou and left his son Yanchang to garrison it, then pressed on to besiege Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 清海留後劉隱發兵擊走之，乘勝進攻韶州。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, acting commissioner of Qinghai, raised troops, drove him off, and pressed the advantage to attack Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, acting commissioner of Qinghai, marched out, routed him, and pursued the victory against Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 隱弟陟以為延昌右虔州之援，未可遽取。

translations.literal: Yin's brother Zhi held that Yanchang had Qianzhou as his right-hand support and could not be taken in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's brother Zhi argued that with Qianzhou backing Yanchang, Shaozhou could not be seized in a rush.

sentences.zh: 隱下從，逐圍韶州。

translations.literal: Yin accepted the advice and turned to besiege Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin agreed and redirected the siege to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會江漲，饋運不繼，光稠自虔州引兵救之。

translations.literal: Just then the river rose and supply transport could not keep up; Guangchou led troops from Qianzhou to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers swelled, supplies failed, and Guangchou marched from Qianzhou to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 其將譚全播伏精兵萬人於山谷，以羸弱挑戰，大破隱於城南，隱奔還。

translations.literal: His general Tan Quanbo hid ten thousand elite troops in a mountain valley, baited the enemy with a weak force, and routed Yin south of the city; Yin fled back.
translations.idiomatic: His general Tan Quanbo concealed ten thousand picked troops in a valley, drew the enemy with a feigned weak force, and shattered Yin south of the city; Yin fled homeward.

sentences.zh: 全播悉以功讓諸將，光稠益賢之。

translations.literal: Quanbo credited all the merit to the other generals; Guangchou esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbo ascribed the whole victory to his fellow commanders, and Guangchou valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 岳州刺史鄧進思卒，弟進忠自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Deng Jinsi, prefect of Yuezhou, died; his younger brother Jinzhong declared himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jinsi, prefect of Yuezhou, died, and his younger brother Jinzhong proclaimed himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝中之下天復三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Brilliant, and Cultured Filial, middle section, second part—Tianfu year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Brilliant, and Cultured Filial, middle section, second part—Tianfu year 3 (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元九零三年）

translations.literal: guihai cycle, corresponding to the year 903 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guihai cycle, corresponding to 903 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲辰，遣殿中侍御史崔構、供奉官郭遵誨詣朱全忠營。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiachen day, Palace Diarist Cui Gou and Palace Attendant Guo Zunhui were sent to Zhu Quanzhong's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on jiachen day the court dispatched Palace Diarist Cui Gou and Palace Attendant Guo Zunhui to Zhu Quanzhong's camp.

sentences.zh: 丙午，李茂貞亦遣牙將郭啟期往議和解。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, Li Maozhen also sent his staff officer Guo Qiqi to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Maozhen too sent his staff officer Guo Qiqi to discuss reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使王師範，頗好學，以忠義自許，為治有聲跡。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan, military governor of Pinglu, was fond of learning, held himself to loyalty and righteousness, and governed with a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan, military governor of Pinglu, loved learning, styled himself a man of loyalty and righteousness, and governed to wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠圍鳳翔，韓全誨以詔書征籓鎮兵入援乘輿，師範見之，泣下沾衿，曰：「吾屬為帝室籓屏，豈得坐視天子困辱如此。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang, Han Quanhui used an imperial edict to summon feudatory troops to rescue the imperial carriage. Shifan read it and tears soaked his robe; he said: "We are the imperial house's screen of defense—how can we sit by while the Son of Heaven suffers such distress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang, Han Quanhui issued an edict summoning feudatory armies to rescue the emperor. Shifan wept until his collar was wet and said, "We are the throne's shield—how can we watch the Son of Heaven endure such humiliation.

sentences.zh: 各擁強兵，但自衛乎！」

translations.literal: Each holds strong troops—yet only to guard himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Each of us commands a powerful army, yet we do nothing but look to our own safety!

sentences.zh: 會張濬自長水亦遺之書，勸舉義兵。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Jun also sent a letter from Changshui urging him to raise a righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: About then Zhang Jun sent a letter from Changshui as well, urging him to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 師範曰：「張公言正會吾意，夫復何疑！

translations.literal: Shifan said: "Lord Zhang's words hit exactly what I mean—what further doubt is there!
translations.idiomatic: Shifan said, "Lord Zhang speaks my mind exactly—what is there to hesitate over!

sentences.zh: 雖力不足，當死生以之。」

translations.literal: Though our strength is insufficient, I shall stake life and death on it."
translations.idiomatic: Even if our strength falls short, I will stake my life on it.

sentences.zh: 時關東兵多從全忠在鳳翔，師範分遣諸將詐為貢獻及商販，包束兵仗，載以小車，入汴、徐、兗、鄆、齊、沂、河南、孟、滑、河中、陝、虢、華等州，期以同日俱發，討全忠。

translations.literal: At that time most eastern troops followed Quanzhong at Fengxiang; Shifan sent his generals separately, disguised as tribute bearers and merchants, packing weapons and loading them on small carts into the prefectures of Bian, Xu, Yan, Yun, Qi, Yi, Henan, Meng, Hua, Hezhong, Shan, Guo, and Hua, planning to rise on the same day and strike at Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Most eastern troops were with Quanzhong at Fengxiang. Shifan dispatched his generals in disguise—as tribute missions and merchants—packing arms on small carts into Bian, Xu, Yan, Yun, Qi, Yi, Henan, Meng, Hua, Hezhong, Shan, Guo, Hua, and other prefectures, intending a simultaneous rising against Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 適諸州者多事洩被擒，獨行軍司馬劉鄩取兗州。

translations.literal: But in most prefectures the plot leaked and men were captured; only the marching commander Liu Yan took Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In most prefectures the scheme leaked and the men were seized; only marching commander Liu Yan seized Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時泰寧節度使葛從周悉將其屯邢州，鄩先遣人為販油者入城，詗其虛實及兵所從入。

translations.literal: At the time Ge Congzhou, military governor of Taining, had led all his garrison troops to Xingzhou; Yan first sent men posing as oil peddlers into the city to scout its condition and the route by which troops could enter.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, military governor of Taining, had then marched his entire garrison to Xingzhou. Yan first sent men disguised as oil sellers into the city to probe its defenses and the point of entry.

sentences.zh: 丙午，鄩將精兵五百夜自水竇入，比明，軍城悉定，市人皆不知。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, Yan led five hundred picked troops by night through the water sluice; by dawn the military city was entirely secured, and the townspeople knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Yan led five hundred elite troops at night through the water gate; by dawn the garrison city was fully in his hands, and the townspeople never knew.

sentences.zh: 鄩據府捨，拜從周母，每旦省竭；

translations.literal: Yan occupied the headquarters, bowed to Congzhou's mother, and visited her each morning with utmost respect;
translations.idiomatic: Yan took the governor's compound, paid respects to Congzhou's mother, and attended her each dawn;

sentences.zh: 待其妻子，甚有恩禮；

translations.literal: he treated Congzhou's wife and children with great kindness and courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: he treated Congzhou's wife and children with marked kindness;

sentences.zh: 子弟職掌、供億如故。

translations.literal: the sons' posts and provisions remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: the sons kept their offices and allowances unchanged.

sentences.zh: 是日，青州牙將張居厚帥壯士二百將小車至華州東城，知州事婁敬思疑其有異，剖視之。

translations.literal: That day, Zhang Juhou, a Qingzhou staff officer, led two hundred stalwarts with small carts to the east wall of Hua Prefecture; Lou Jingsi, acting prefect, suspected something amiss and cut open the bundles to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhang Juhou, a Qingzhou staff officer, led two hundred toughs with small carts to Hua Prefecture's east wall; Lou Jingsi, acting prefect, grew suspicious and sliced open the bundles.

sentences.zh: 其徒大呼，殺敬思，攻西城。

translations.literal: His men shouted; they killed Jingsi and attacked the west wall.
translations.idiomatic: The men raised a cry, killed Jingsi, and stormed the west wall.

sentences.zh: 崔胤在華州，帥眾拒之，不克，走至商州，追獲之。

translations.literal: Cui Yin was at Hua Prefecture and led the crowd to resist them but could not prevail; they fled to Shang Prefecture and were pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was in Hua Prefecture and led the people in resistance but failed; the raiders fled toward Shang Prefecture and were run down and captured.

sentences.zh: 全忠留節度判官裴迪守大梁，師範遣走卒繼書至大梁，迪問以東方事，走卒色動。

translations.literal: Quanzhong left Pei Di, his military governor's judge, to hold Daliang; Shifan sent a runner with a letter to Daliang, and when Di asked about affairs in the east, the runner's face changed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong left his governor's judge Pei Di to hold Daliang. Shifan sent a runner with a letter; when Di asked about the east, the runner's face betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 迪察其有變，屏人問之，走卒具以實告。

translations.literal: Di perceived that something was afoot; dismissing attendants, he questioned the runner, who told him everything.
translations.idiomatic: Di sensed trouble, dismissed the room, and pressed the runner, who confessed the whole plot.

sentences.zh: 迪不暇白全忠，亟請馬步都指揮使朱友寧將兵萬餘人東巡兗、鄆。

translations.literal: Without waiting to report to Quanzhong, Di urgently requested that Zhu Youning, commander of horse and foot, lead more than ten thousand troops east to patrol Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Without reporting to Quanzhong, Di urgently asked Zhu Youning, commander of horse and foot, to lead more than ten thousand men east to patrol Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 友寧召葛從周於邢州，共攻師範。

translations.literal: Youning summoned Ge Congzhou from Xingzhou, and together they attacked Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Youning called Ge Congzhou down from Xingzhou, and the two marched against Shifan.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞變，亦分兵先歸，使友寧並將之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard of the revolt and also split his forces to return first, putting Youning in overall command.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong learned of the uprising he too sent part of his army back ahead of him and placed Youning in supreme command.

sentences.zh: 戊申，李茂貞獨見上，中尉韓全誨、張彥弘、樞密使袁易簡、周敬容皆不得對。

translations.literal: On wushen day, Li Maozhen alone received audience; Chief Eunuchs Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong, and Privy Councilors Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong, were all denied access.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Maozhen saw the emperor alone; Chief Eunuchs Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong and Privy Councilors Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong were barred from the audience.

sentences.zh: 茂貞請誅全誨等，與朱全忠和解，奉車駕還京。

translations.literal: Maozhen requested execution of Quanhui and the others, reconciliation with Zhu Quanzhong, and escorting the imperial carriage back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen asked that Quanhui and his circle be executed, that peace be made with Zhu Quanzhong, and that the emperor be escorted back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上喜，即遣內養帥鳳翔卒四十人收全誨等，斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced and immediately sent inner attendants leading forty Fengxiang soldiers to seize Quanhui and the others and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and at once sent inner attendants at the head of forty Fengxiang soldiers to seize Quanhui and the rest and behead them.

sentences.zh: 以御食使弟五可范為左軍中尉，宣徽南院使仇承坦為右軍中尉，王知古為上院樞密使，楊虔朗為下院樞密使。

translations.literal: Diwu Kefan, younger brother of the Imperial Food Commissioner, was made Left Chief Eunuch; Qiu Chengtan, Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, was made Right Chief Eunuch; Wang Zhigu was made Upper Privy Councilor, and Yang Qianlang Lower Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Kefan, younger brother of the Imperial Food Commissioner, was appointed Left Chief Eunuch; Qiu Chengtan, commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, Right Chief Eunuch; Wang Zhigu upper Privy Councilor; and Yang Qianlang lower Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 是夕，又斬李繼筠、李繼誨、李彥弼及內諸司使韋處廷等十六人。

translations.literal: That evening Li Jiyun, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and sixteen others including Inner Palace Bureau Commissioner Wei Chuting were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Li Jiyun, Li Jihui, Li Yanbi, and sixteen others including Inner Palace Bureau Commissioner Wei Chuting were beheaded as well.

sentences.zh: 己酉，遣韓偓及趙國夫人詣全忠營，又遣使囊全誨等二十餘人首以示全忠，曰：「曏來脅留車駕，懼罪離間，不欲協和，皆此曹也。

translations.literal: On jiyou day, Han Wo and the Lady of Zhao State were sent to Quanzhong's camp, and envoys were also dispatched with the heads of Quanhui and more than twenty others to show Quanzhong, saying: "In the past the imperial carriage was detained under coercion; fearing guilt, they sowed discord and would not agree to peace—all of this was these men's doing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Han Wo and the Lady of Zhao State were sent to Quanzhong's camp, and messengers carried the heads of Quanhui and more than twenty others to show him, with this message: "These men coerced the emperor's detention, then feared punishment and blocked peace—

sentences.zh: 今朕與茂貞決意誅之，卿可曉諭諸軍，以豁眾憤。」

translations.literal: Now I and Maozhen have resolved to execute them; you may explain this to the armies and dispel the troops' anger."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen and I have now killed them. Explain this to the armies and ease the soldiers' wrath."

sentences.zh: 辛亥，全忠遣觀察判官李振奉表入謝。

translations.literal: On xinhai day, Quanzhong sent his observation judge Li Zhen to submit a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Quanzhong sent his observation judge Li Zhen to present a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 全誨等已誅，而全忠圍猶未解。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others had been executed, yet Quanzhong's siege was still not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and his circle were dead, yet Quanzhong's siege remained.

sentences.zh: 茂貞疑崔胤教全忠欲必取鳳翔，白上急召胤，令帥百官赴行在。

translations.literal: Maozhen suspected Cui Yin had coached Quanzhong to insist on taking Fengxiang; he told the emperor to summon Yin urgently and ordered him to lead the hundred officials to the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen suspected Cui Yin had urged Quanzhong to demand Fengxiang outright; he told the emperor to summon Yin at once and ordered him to bring the hundred officials to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 凡四降詔，三賜朱書御札，言甚切至，悉復故官爵，胤竟稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Four edicts were issued in all, and three imperial letters in vermilion ink with words of utmost urgency restored all former offices and titles, yet Yin still pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Four edicts went out, and three vermilion imperial letters, urgent and pleading, restored every former rank—but Yin still pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 茂貞懼，自致書於胤，辭甚卑遜。

translations.literal: Maozhen grew afraid and himself wrote Yin a letter, the wording very humble and deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen grew afraid and wrote Yin himself, in the most abject terms.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦以書召胤，且戲之曰：「吾未識天子，須公來辨其是非。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong also summoned Yin by letter and jested: "I have never met the Son of Heaven; I need you to come and tell right from wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong summoned Yin as well and teased him: "I have never met the emperor; I need you to tell me whether he is real or not.

sentences.zh: 胤始來。

translations.literal: Only then did Yin come.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yin set out.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，鳳翔始啟城門。

translations.literal: On jiayin day, Fengxiang at last opened the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Fengxiang finally opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，全忠巡諸寨，至城北，有鳳翔兵自北山下，全忠疑其逼己，遣兵擊之，擒其將李繼欽。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, Quanzhong inspected the camps; reaching the north of the city, Fengxiang troops came down from the northern hills. Quanzhong suspected they were pressing him and sent troops to strike them, capturing their general Li Jiqin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Quanzhong toured the camps. Near the north wall, Fengxiang troops descended from the northern hills; Quanzhong took it for an attack on him and sent men to strike them, capturing their commander Li Jiqin.

sentences.zh: 上遣趙國夫人、馮翊夫人詣全忠營詰其故，全忠遣親吏蔣玄暉奉表入奏。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Lady of Zhao State and the Lady of Fenyang to Quanzhong's camp to demand the reason; Quanzhong sent his personal clerk Jiang Xuanhui to submit a memorial explaining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Lady of Zhao State and the Lady of Fenyang to Quanzhong's camp to demand an explanation; Quanzhong dispatched his personal clerk Jiang Xuanhui to memorialize the court.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞請以其子侃尚平原公主，又欲以蘇檢女為景王秘妃以自固。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen requested that his son Kan marry Princess Pingyuan, and also wished to make Su Jian's daughter consort to Prince Jing to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen asked that his son Kan marry Princess Pingyuan and also sought to install Su Jian's daughter as Prince Jing's consort to strengthen his position.

sentences.zh: 平原公主，何-{后}-之女也，-{后}-意難之。

translations.literal: Princess Pingyuan was the daughter of Empress He; the empress found the match hard to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Pingyuan was Empress He's daughter, and the empress balked at the match.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「且令我得出，何憂爾女！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Once you let me out, what worry is there for your daughter!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Once I am free of this place, what need to worry over your daughter!

sentences.zh: 後乃從之。

translations.literal: Only afterward did she consent.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did she agree.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，平原公主嫁宋侃。

translations.literal: On renxu day, Princess Pingyuan married Song Kan.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Princess Pingyuan was married to Song Kan.

sentences.zh: 納景王妃蘇氏。

translations.literal: Lady Su was received as consort to Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su of the Su clan was taken in as Prince Jing's consort.

sentences.zh: 時鳳翔所誅宦官已七十二人，朱全忠又密令京兆搜捕致仕不從行者，誅九十人。

translations.literal: By then seventy-two eunuchs had already been executed at Fengxiang; Zhu Quanzhong also secretly ordered the capital prefecture to hunt down retired eunuchs who had not followed the emperor into exile, and ninety were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: By then seventy-two eunuchs had already been killed at Fengxiang; Zhu Quanzhong also secretly ordered the capital prefect to hunt down retired eunuchs who had not followed the court into exile, and ninety more were executed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，車駕出鳳翔，幸全忠營，全忠素服待罪。

translations.literal: On jiazi day, the imperial carriage left Fengxiang and visited Quanzhong's camp; Quanzhong wore plain dress awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor left Fengxiang and entered Quanzhong's camp; Quanzhong met him in undyed mourning garb, awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 命客省使宣旨釋罪，去三仗，止報平安，以公服入謝。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Guest Reception Commissioner to announce an edict absolving guilt, to remove the three ceremonial guards, to report only "all is well," and to enter in official court dress to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Guest Reception Commissioner to announce absolution, dispense with the three ceremonial guards, require only a report of "peace," and admit Quanzhong in court dress to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 全忠見上，頓首流涕。

translations.literal: Quanzhong saw the emperor, kowtowed, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw the emperor, kowtowed, and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 上命韓偓扶起之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Han Wo to help him rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Han Wo to raise him up.

sentences.zh: 上亦泣，曰：「宗廟社稷，賴卿再安；

translations.literal: The emperor wept as well and said: "The altars of state rely on you for restoration once again;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept too and said, "The altars of state owe their restoration to you;

sentences.zh: 朕與宗族，賴卿再生。」

translations.literal: I and the imperial clan rely on you for rebirth."
translations.idiomatic: I and my kin owe you our lives.

sentences.zh: 親解玉帶以賜之。

translations.literal: He personally unfastened his jade belt and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: With that he unfastened his jade belt and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 少休，即行。

translations.literal: After a brief rest, they set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: After a short rest they departed at once.

sentences.zh: 全忠單騎前導十許裡，上辭之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong rode alone ahead as guide for some ten li; the emperor declined this.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong rode alone ahead for some ten li as escort; the emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃令朱友倫將兵扈從，自留部分後隊，焚撤諸寨。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then ordered Zhu Youlun to lead troops as escort, while he himself remained with the rear guard, burning and dismantling the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then put Zhu Youlun in command of the escort while he stayed behind with the rear guard, burning and breaking up the camps.

sentences.zh: 友倫，存之子也。

translations.literal: Youlun was the son of Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Youlun was Zhu Cun's son.

sentences.zh: 是夕，車駕宿岐山。

translations.literal: That evening the imperial carriage lodged at Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor slept at Qishan.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至興平，崔胤始帥百官迎謁，復以胤為司空、門下侍郎、同平章事，領三司如故。

translations.literal: On dingmao day they reached Xingping; Cui Yin at last led the hundred officials to welcome and pay homage, and Yin was again made Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister, continuing to head the Three Fiscal Agencies as before.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day they reached Xingping; Cui Yin at last led the hundred officials out to welcome them, and Yin was restored as Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister, and head of the Three Fiscal Agencies.

sentences.zh: 己巳，入長安。

translations.literal: On jisi day, they entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day they entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 庚午，全忠、崔胤同對。

translations.literal: On gengwu day, Quanzhong and Cui Yin attended audience together.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Quanzhong and Cui Yin attended audience together.

sentences.zh: 胤奏：「國初承平之時，宦官不典兵預政。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized: "In the early peace of the founding, eunuchs did not command troops or take part in government.
translations.idiomatic: Yin memorialized: "At the founding, in times of peace, eunuchs neither commanded troops nor meddled in government.

sentences.zh: 天寶以來，宦官浸盛。

translations.literal: Since the Tianbao era, eunuchs gradually grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao era onward, eunuch power steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 貞元之末，分羽林衛為左、右神策軍以便衛從，始令宦官主之，以二千人為定制。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, the Imperial Guard was split into Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies for convenient imperial escort, and eunuchs were first made to command them, with two thousand men as the fixed establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenyuan reign, the Imperial Guard was divided into the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies to serve as the emperor's escort, and eunuchs were placed in command for the first time, with a fixed strength of two thousand men each.

sentences.zh: 自是參掌機密，奪百司權，上下彌縫，共為不法，大則構扇籓鎮，傾危國家；

translations.literal: From this they shared in secret affairs, seized the authority of the hundred offices, patched over matters high and low, and together engaged in unlawful deeds; on a large scale they incited and fomented the frontier governors and endangered the state;
translations.idiomatic: From then on they shared in confidential affairs, stripped the hundred offices of their powers, covered for one another from top to bottom, and together broke the law; at their worst they stirred up the military governors and shook the state to its foundations;

sentences.zh: 小則賣官鬻獄，蠹害朝政。

translations.literal: on a small scale they sold offices and trafficked in judgments, corrupting and harming court governance.
translations.idiomatic: at their petty worst they sold offices and judgments, poisoning the governance of the court.

sentences.zh: 王室衰亂，職此之由，不翦其根，禍終不已。

translations.literal: The royal house's decline and disorder owed chiefly to this; if the root were not cut, disaster would never end.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's decline sprang chiefly from this; unless the root were cut away, calamity would never cease.

sentences.zh: 請悉罷內諸司使，其事務盡歸之省寺，諸道監軍俱召還闕下。」

translations.literal: I request that all the inner palace bureau commissioners be entirely abolished, their affairs wholly returned to the ministries and courts, and the army supervisors in every circuit all summoned back to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all the inner palace commissioners be abolished outright, that their business be returned entirely to the ministries and courts, and that the army supervisors in every circuit be recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠以兵驅宦官第五可范等數百人於內侍省，盡殺之，冤號之聲，徹於內外。

translations.literal: That day, Quanzhong with troops drove several hundred eunuchs including Diwu Kefan into the Palace Domestic Service Office and killed them all; cries of grievance and wailing pierced inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Quanzhong used troops to drive several hundred eunuchs, including Diwu Kefan, into the Palace Domestic Service Office and slaughtered them all; wails of injustice echoed throughout the palace and beyond.

sentences.zh: 出使外方者，詔所在收捕誅之，止留黃衣幼弱者三十人以備灑掃。

translations.literal: Those serving on missions abroad were ordered seized and executed wherever found; only thirty youths in yellow robes, weak and young, were kept for sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: Those on assignment outside the capital were ordered seized and executed wherever found; only thirty young eunuchs in yellow robes were kept for menial service.

sentences.zh: 又詔成德節度使王鎔選進五十人充敕使，取其土風深厚、人性謹樸也。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Chengde military governor Wang Rong to select and send up fifty men to serve as imperial envoys, taking their region's deep local custom and people's cautious plainness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Wang Rong, military governor of Chengde, to select and send up fifty men to serve as imperial messengers, chosen for the region's solid local ways and its people's plain, sober character.

sentences.zh: 上愍可范等或無罪，為文祭之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied Kefan and the others, who might have been guiltless, and composed a text to sacrifice to them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, believing that Kefan and the others might have been innocent, wrote a memorial text to mourn them.

sentences.zh: 自是宣傳詔命，皆令宮人出入。

translations.literal: From this, proclaiming and transmitting imperial edicts all employed palace women to come and go.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the delivery of imperial edicts was entrusted entirely to palace women.

sentences.zh: 其兩軍內外八鎮兵悉屬六軍，以崔胤兼判六軍十二衛事。

translations.literal: The troops of both armies and the eight garrisons inside and outside all fell under the Six Armies, and Cui Yin was made concurrently to adjudicate the affairs of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The forces of both Divine Strategy Armies and the eight garrison commands, inner and outer, were placed under the Six Armies, and Cui Yin was given concurrent charge of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：宦官用權，為國家患，其來久矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Eunuchs wielding power and becoming a calamity to the state is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang observes: Eunuch power has long been a plague upon the state.

sentences.zh: 蓋以出入宮禁，人主自幼及長，與之親狎，非如三公六卿，進見有時，可嚴憚也。

translations.literal: For they enter and leave the palace precincts; the ruler from youth to maturity is intimate and familiar with them—not like the Three Dukes and Six Ministers, whose audiences come at fixed times and inspire solemn awe.
translations.idiomatic: Because they move in and out of the inner palace, the ruler grows up among them in daily intimacy—nothing like the Three Dukes and Six Ministers, whose audiences are scheduled and who inspire due awe.

sentences.zh: 其間復有性識儇利，語言辯給，善伺候顏色，承迎志趣，受命則無違遷之忠，使令則有稱愜之效。

translations.literal: Among them are also those of nimble wit and keen intelligence, eloquent in speech, skilled at reading expressions and meeting desires; charged with a duty they show no loyal reluctance, and given an order they produce pleasing results.
translations.idiomatic: Some among them are quick-witted and sharp-tongued, expert at reading a face and catching a mood; when tasked they never show the loyalty that resists a command, and when ordered they deliver exactly what pleases.

sentences.zh: 自非上智之主，燭知物情，慮患深遠，侍奉之外，不任以事，則近者日親，遠者日疏，甘言悲辭之請有時而從，浸潤膚受之訴有時而聽。

translations.literal: Unless the ruler is of supreme intelligence, discerning human affairs, and far-sighted in foreseeing harm, and beyond attendance employs them in no business, then those near grow daily closer, those far grow daily distant; requests in sweet words and tearful pleas are sometimes granted, and grievances whispered close are sometimes heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the ruler is exceptionally wise—seeing through men, thinking far ahead, and employing eunuchs for attendance alone and for nothing else—those nearest grow ever closer while honest ministers drift away; honeyed pleas and tearful appeals win a hearing, and private grievances soaked in by steady repetition find a willing ear.

sentences.zh: 於是黜陟刑賞之政，潛移於近習而不自知，如飲醇酒，嗜其味而忘其醉也。

translations.literal: Then the policies of dismissal, promotion, punishment, and reward silently shift to the ruler's intimate attendants without his knowing it, like drinking rich wine, relishing the flavor and forgetting the drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Before he knows it, the power to appoint, dismiss, punish, and reward has shifted to his intimates—like a man sipping fine wine, savoring the taste and forgetting that he is drunk.

sentences.zh: 黜陟刑賞之柄移而國家不危亂者，未之有也。

translations.literal: When the handles of dismissal, promotion, punishment, and reward shift, and the state does not fall into peril and disorder—never has such a thing existed.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a state remained secure once the power of appointment, dismissal, punishment, and reward changed hands.

sentences.zh: 東漢之衰，宦官最名驕橫，然皆假人主之權，依憑城社，以濁亂天下，未有能劫脅天子如制嬰兒，廢置在手。

translations.literal: In Eastern Han's decline, eunuchs were most notorious for arrogance and overbearing conduct, yet all borrowed the lord's authority, relying on city altars, to muddy and disorder the realm; none could seize and coerce the Son of Heaven as one controls an infant, with deposition and installation in hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the decline of Eastern Han, eunuchs were notorious for arrogance, yet they still only borrowed the emperor's authority and leaned on the power of office to corrupt the realm; none could seize the emperor as one seizes an infant, with enthronement and deposition in their own hands.

sentences.zh: 東西出其意，使天子畏之若乘虎狼而挾蛇虺如唐世者也。

translations.literal: Coming and going at their whim, making the Son of Heaven fear them as if riding tigers and wolves while clutching vipers and serpents—such was the Tang age.
translations.idiomatic: They moved at will, leaving the emperor in terror as if riding among tigers and wolves with serpents coiled in his lap—such was Tang.

sentences.zh: 所以然者非它，漢不握兵，唐握兵故也。

translations.literal: The reason is nothing else: Han did not hold the army, Tang held the army.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is simple: Han eunuchs did not command troops; Tang eunuchs did.

sentences.zh: 太宗鑒前世之弊，深抑宦官無得過四品。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong took warning from previous ages' ills and deeply restrained eunuchs from exceeding the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, taking warning from earlier ages, strictly capped eunuchs at the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 明皇始隳舊章，是崇是長，晚節令高力士省決章奏，乃至進退將相，時與之議，自太子王公皆畏事之，宦官自此熾矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming began to destroy the old statutes, exalting and fostering them; in his later years he had Gao Lishi review and decide memorials, even to advancing and dismissing generals and chancellors, sometimes deliberating with him; from the crown prince to the princes and dukes, all feared and served him—eunuchs from this blazed up.
translations.idiomatic: Minghuang was the first to break the old rules, lavishing favor upon them; in his later years he had Gao Lishi screen and decide memorials, even disposing of generals and chancellors, sometimes consulting him in the matter; from the crown prince to the princes, all feared and deferred to him—and eunuch power blazed up from that point.

sentences.zh: 及中原板蕩，肅宗收兵靈武，李輔國以東宮舊隸參豫軍謀，寵過而驕，不復能制，遂至愛子慈父皆不能庇，以憂悸終。

translations.literal: When the Central Plain was churned in turmoil, Emperor Suzong gathered troops at Lingwu; Li Fuguo, an old attendant from the Eastern Palace, took part in military planning; favored beyond measure, he grew arrogant and could no longer be controlled, until loving son and fond father alike could not protect each other, and Suzong ended in anxiety and dread.
translations.idiomatic: When the central plains were thrown into chaos, Suzong rallied his armies at Lingwu; Li Fuguo, a former Eastern Palace servant, joined in military planning, and once over-favored grew too proud to be controlled, until neither loving son nor fond father could shelter the other, and Suzong died of dread and grief.

sentences.zh: 代宗踐阼，仍遵覆轍，程元振、魚朝恩相繼用事，竊弄刑賞，壅蔽聰明，視天子如委裘，陵宰相如奴虜，是以來瑱入朝，遇讒賜死。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong ascended the throne yet followed the overturned track; Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en successively held power, stealthily manipulating punishments and rewards, blocking and hiding clear vision, treating the Son of Heaven like a discarded robe, and bullying chancellors like slaves and captives—thus when Lai Tian entered court, slander met him and he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong took the throne yet walked the same ruinous path; Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en wielded power in turn, stealing control of punishments and rewards, blinding the emperor to truth, treating the throne like a cast-off garment and chancellors like bondsmen—so when Lai Tian came to court, slander reached him and he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃深侵郊甸，匿不以聞，致狼狽幸陝。

translations.literal: Tibetans deeply invaded the suburbs; this was concealed and not reported, causing disarray and the emperor's flight to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided deep into the capital's outskirts, yet the news was suppressed, leaving the court in chaos and forcing the emperor's frantic flight to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 李光弼危疑憤郁，以損其生。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi, in peril, doubt, anger, and gloom, shortened his life thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi, hemmed in by suspicion and swallowed by rage, died of it.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀擯廢家居，不保丘壟。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was cast aside and retired home, unable even to protect his ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was pushed aside and sent home, unable even to guard his family graves.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩冤抑無訴，遂棄勳庸，更為叛亂。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en, wronged and suppressed with no recourse, then abandoned his merits and turned to rebellion instead.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en, unjustly humiliated and with no one to hear him, abandoned his honors and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 德宗初立，頗振綱紀，宦官稍絀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong first ascended, he somewhat restored discipline, and eunuchs were slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first took the throne he revived discipline somewhat, and eunuch influence ebbed a little.

sentences.zh: 而返自興元，猜忌諸將，以李晟、渾瑊為不可信，悉奪其兵，而以竇文場、霍仙鳴為中尉，使典宿衛，自是太阿之柄，落其掌握矣。

translations.literal: Yet returning from Xingyuan, suspecting the generals and deeming Li Sheng and Hun Jian untrustworthy, he stripped them all of their troops and made Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming army supervisors, putting them in charge of the palace guard—from this the sword's hilt fell into their grasp.
translations.idiomatic: But after returning from Xingyuan he grew suspicious of his generals, judged Li Sheng and Hun Jian untrustworthy, stripped them of command, and made Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming army supervisors over the palace guard—from that moment the sword hilt passed into eunuch hands.

sentences.zh: 憲宗末年，吐突承璀欲廢嫡立庶，以成陳洪志之變。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzong's final years, Tuhu Chenghui wished to depose the heir and install a lesser son, bringing about the affair of Chen Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong's last years Tuhu Chenghui tried to set aside the heir in favor of a younger son, leading to Chen Hongzhi's coup.

sentences.zh: 寶歷狎暱群小，劉克明與蘇佐明為逆，其後絳王及文、武、宣、懿、僖、昭六帝，皆為宦官所立，勢益驕橫。

translations.literal: In Baoli, intimacy with petty men; Liu Keming and Su Zuoming rebelled; thereafter Prince Jiang and the six emperors Wenzong, Wuzong, Xuanzong, Yizong, Xizong, and Zhaozong were all installed by eunuchs, and their power grew ever more arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Baoli the court doted on petty favorites; Liu Keming and Su Zuoming plotted treason; thereafter Prince Jiang and six emperors—Wenzong, Wuzong, Xuanzong, Yizong, Xizong, and Zhaozong—were all put on the throne by eunuchs, and eunuch power grew ever more insolent.

sentences.zh: 王守澄、仇士良、田令孜、楊復恭、劉季述、韓全誨為之魁傑。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng, Qiu Shiliang, Tian Lingzi, Yang Fugong, Liu Jishu, and Han Quanhui were its leading giants.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng, Qiu Shiliang, Tian Lingzi, Yang Fugong, Liu Jishu, and Han Quanhui were the worst of them.

sentences.zh: 至自稱「定策國老」，目天子為門生，根深蒂固，疾成膏肓，不可救藥矣！

translations.literal: They went so far as to style themselves "Elder of the State Who Fixed the Succession," regarded the Son of Heaven as their student, with roots deep and stem firm, sickness becoming vital organs, beyond saving by medicine!
translations.idiomatic: They even styled themselves "Elders Who Fixed the Succession," looked upon the emperor as their disciple, put down roots too deep to pull up, and sank their poison into the dynasty's vital organs until it was past cure!

sentences.zh: 文宗深憤其然，志欲除之，以宋申錫之賢，猶不能有所為，反受其殃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong deeply resented this, resolved to eliminate them; yet even with Song Shenxi's worth, he still could accomplish nothing, and instead suffered calamity from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong hated this deeply and resolved to destroy them; yet even with a man as worthy as Song Shenxi he could do nothing—and paid for the attempt with his ruin.

sentences.zh: 況李訓、鄭注反覆小人，欲以一朝譎詐之謀，翦累世膠固之黨，遂至涉血禁塗，積屍省戶，公卿大臣，連頸就誅，闔門屠滅，天子陽瘖縱酒，飲泣吞氣，自比赧、獻，不亦悲乎！

translations.literal: How much less Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, fickle petty men, who wished with one morning's treacherous plot to cut down a party cemented through generations—until blood soaked the forbidden paths, corpses piled at provincial gates, great ministers and high officials were beheaded in a row, whole clans slaughtered, and the Son of Heaven pretended muteness and drowned himself in wine, swallowing tears and rage, comparing himself to King Nan and Emperor Xian—is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: What then of Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, shifty petty schemers who thought one morning's conspiracy could uproot a faction hardened over generations—until blood flooded the forbidden avenues, corpses heaped at the ministry gates, ministers were led off to slaughter in chains, whole families were wiped out, and the emperor feigned dumbness and drowned his sorrow in wine, likening himself to the last kings of Zhou and Han—was it not pitiable!

sentences.zh: 以宣宗之嚴毅明察，猶閉目搖首，自謂畏之。

translations.literal: Even with Emperor Xuanzong's sternness, resolution, and perspicacity, he still shut his eyes and shook his head, saying himself that he feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Even Xuanzong, stern, resolute, and sharp-eyed, would shut his eyes and shake his head, admitting that he feared them.

sentences.zh: 況懿、僖之驕侈，苟聲色球獵足充其欲，則政事一以付之，呼之以父，固無怪矣。

translations.literal: How much less Yizong and Xizong, arrogant and extravagant—provided music, women, polo, and hunting sufficed their desires, they entrusted all government to eunuchs and called them "Father"—no wonder indeed.
translations.idiomatic: What then of Yizong and Xizong, vain and self-indulgent? Once music, women, sport, and the hunt satisfied their appetites, they handed all government over to eunuchs and called them "Father"—small wonder.

sentences.zh: 賊污宮闕，兩幸梁、益，皆令孜所為也。

translations.literal: Rebellions defiling the palace, two flights to Liang and Yi—all were Tian Lingzi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels staining the palace, the emperor's two flights to Liang and Yi—all were Tian Lingzi's work.

sentences.zh: 昭宗不勝其恥，力欲清滌，而所任不得其人，所行不由其道。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, unable to bear the shame, strove to cleanse and purge, yet those he employed were not the right men, and what he did did not follow the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong, unable to bear the humiliation, strove to purge the court—but chose the wrong men and pursued the wrong course.

sentences.zh: 始則張濬覆軍於平陽，增李克用跋扈之勢；

translations.literal: At first Zhang Jun destroyed his army at Pingyang, increasing Li Keyong's overbearing momentum;
translations.idiomatic: First Zhang Jun lost his army at Pingyang, only strengthening Li Keyong's arrogance;

sentences.zh: 復恭亡命於山南，啟宋文通不臣之心；

translations.literal: Yang Fugong fled for his life into Shannan, opening Song Wentong's heart of disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong fled into the mountains south of the capital, awakening disloyalty in Song Wentong;

sentences.zh: 終則兵交闕庭，矢及御衣，漂泊莎城，流寓華陰，幽辱東內，劫遷岐陽。

translations.literal: In the end arms clashed at the palace gate, arrows reached the emperor's robe; drifting at Sha City, sojourning at Huayin, confined and shamed in the Eastern Inner Palace, seized and removed to Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the end weapons clashed at the palace gates and arrows pierced the emperor's robe; he was driven to wander at Sha City, lodge at Huayin, endure imprisonment in the Eastern Palace, and be seized and moved to Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 崔昌遐無如之何，更召朱全忠以討之。

translations.literal: Cui Changxia could do nothing about it and again summoned Zhu Quanzhong to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Changxia could find no remedy and again summoned Zhu Quanzhong to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 連兵圍城，再罹寒暑，御膳不足於糗□，王侯斃踣於饑寒，然後全誨就誅，乘輿東出，翦滅其黨，靡有孑遺，而唐之廟社因以兵墟矣！

translations.literal: Continuous troops besieged the city through two rounds of cold and heat; the imperial table lacked even parched grain □; princes and marquises fell dead from hunger and cold; only then was Quanhui executed, the imperial carriage went east, his faction was cut down and destroyed, not one left alone—and Tang's altars of state thereby became a battlefield ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Troops laid siege through two seasons of cold and heat; even the emperor's table ran short of provisions; princes and nobles collapsed from hunger and cold; only then was Quanhui executed, the emperor marched east, and the eunuch faction was exterminated to the last man—yet Tang's altars of state had already been turned into a wasteland of war!

sentences.zh: 然則宦者之禍，始於明皇，盛於肅、代，成於德宗，極於昭宗。

translations.literal: Thus the eunuchs' calamity began with Minghuang, flourished under Suzong and Daizong, took form under Dezong, and reached its extreme under Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: So the eunuchs' disaster began with Minghuang, swelled under Suzong and Daizong, took shape under Dezong, and reached its climax under Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「履霜堅冰至。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "When treading on frost, solid ice will come."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Tread on frost, and solid ice is not far behind."

sentences.zh: 為國家者，防微杜漸，可不慎其始哉！

translations.literal: For one who governs a state, to guard against the subtle and stop the gradual—can one not be careful at the beginning!
translations.idiomatic: For the ruler of a state, to guard against the small and stop the gradual—how can he fail to be careful at the outset!

sentences.zh: 此其為患，章章尤著者也。

translations.literal: This as a calamity is the most clearly and especially manifest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Of all their harms, this is the most conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 自餘傷賢害能，召亂致禍，賣官鬻獄，沮敗師徒，蠹害烝民，不可遍舉。

translations.literal: The rest—injuring worthies and harming the capable, summoning disorder and bringing calamity, selling offices and trafficking in judgments, obstructing and ruining armies, corrupting and harming the people—cannot be fully enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: The rest—destroying the worthy, inviting rebellion, selling offices and judgments, ruining armies, and devouring the people—cannot all be counted.

sentences.zh: 夫寺人之官，自三王之世，載於詩、禮，所以謹閨闥之禁，通內外之言，安可無也。

translations.literal: Now the office of palace attendants, from the age of the Three Sage-Kings, is recorded in the Book of Songs and Book of Rites, to keep strict the inner quarters' prohibitions and convey words between inside and outside—how could it be dispensed with?
translations.idiomatic: The office of palace attendant dates from the age of the Three Kings; it is recorded in the Songs and the Rites to guard the inner quarters and carry word between palace and court—how could it be abolished?

sentences.zh: 如巷伯之疾惡，寺人披之事君，鄭眾之辭賞，呂□疆之直諫，曹日昇之救患，馬存亮之弭亂，楊復光之討賊，嚴遵美之避權，張承業之竭忠，其中豈無賢才乎！

translations.literal: Such as Xiangbo's hatred of evil, the palace attendant Pi's service to his lord, Zheng Zhong's declining reward, Lü □ Jiang's straight remonstrance, Cao Risheng's rescue from disaster, Ma Cunliang's quelling disorder, Yang Fuguang's punishing rebels, Yan Zunmei's shunning power, Zhang Chengye's exhausting loyalty—among them, are there not worthy talents!
translations.idiomatic: Xiangbo's zeal against evil, the palace attendant Pi's faithful service, Zheng Zhong's refusal of reward, Lü Qiang's blunt remonstrance, Cao Risheng's saving the court in crisis, Ma Cunliang's calming of rebellion, Yang Fuguang's campaign against rebels, Yan Zunmei's refusal of power, Zhang Chengye's steadfast loyalty—among these, were there no able men?

sentences.zh: 顧人主不當與之謀議政事，進退士大夫，使有威福足以動人耳。

translations.literal: Only the ruler ought not to plan and deliberate on government with them, or advance and dismiss scholar-officials, letting them possess authority and favor enough to move others.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ruler ought never to discuss government with them or let them appoint and dismiss officials, giving them power and favor enough to sway the realm.

sentences.zh: 果或有罪，小則刑之，大則誅之，無所寬赦。

translations.literal: If they truly have guilt, for small matters punish them, for great matters execute them—no leniency or pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If one is guilty, punish him for small offenses and execute him for large ones, without mercy.

sentences.zh: 如此，雖使之專橫，孰敢焉！

translations.literal: In this way, even if they were made tyrannical, who would dare!
translations.idiomatic: Then, even were they inclined to arrogance, who would dare defy the throne?

sentences.zh: 豈可不察臧否，不擇是非，欲草薙而禽獮之，能無亂乎！

translations.literal: How can one fail to examine good and bad, fail to choose right and wrong, and wish to mow them down like grass and hunt them like game—can there fail to be disorder!
translations.idiomatic: How can one refuse to distinguish good from bad, right from wrong, and try to mow eunuchs down like weeds or slaughter them like quarry—without breeding chaos?

sentences.zh: 是以袁紹行之於前而董卓弱漢，崔昌遐襲之於後而朱氏篡唐，雖快一時之忿而國隨以亡。

translations.literal: Therefore Yuan Shao did this before and Dong Zhuo enfeebled Han; Cui Changxia followed this after and the Zhu clan usurped Tang—though venting momentary wrath, the state followed into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao tried it first, and Dong Zhuo enfeebled Han; Cui Changxia copied him, and the Zhu house seized Tang—a moment's vengeance, and the state perished with it.

sentences.zh: 是猶惡衣之垢而焚之，患木之蠹而伐之，其為害豈不益多哉！

translations.literal: This is like hating a garment's filth and burning it, or fearing a tree's worms and felling it—the harm done is not rather greater!
translations.idiomatic: That is like burning a filthy robe because one hates the stain, or felling a tree because one fears the worms—the harm done is only greater!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「人而不仁，疾之已甚，亂也。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "A man without humaneness—hate him too fiercely, and there is disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Where there is a man without humanity, to hate him beyond measure is to invite disorder."

sentences.zh: 斯之謂矣！

translations.literal: This is what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: That is the saying!

sentences.zh: 王師範遣使以起兵告李克用，克用貽書褒贊之。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan sent envoys to inform Li Keyong of raising troops; Keyong sent a letter commending and praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan sent envoys to tell Li Keyong that he had taken up arms; Keyong replied with a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 河東監軍張承業亦勸克用發兵救鳳翔，克用攻晉州，聞車駕東歸，乃罷。

translations.literal: Hedong army supervisor Zhang Chengye also urged Keyong to dispatch troops to rescue Fengxiang; Keyong attacked Jin Prefecture, and hearing the imperial carriage was returning east, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye, Hedong's army supervisor, also urged Keyong to march and relieve Fengxiang; Keyong attacked Jin Prefecture, but hearing that the emperor was returning east, he broke off.

sentences.zh: 楊行密承製加朱瑾東面諸道行營副都統、同平章事，以升州刺史李神福為淮南行軍司馬、鄂岳行營招討使，舒州團練使劉存副之，將兵擊杜洪。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi, accepting the imperial edict, added Zhu Jin as deputy overall commander of the eastern circuits' campaign headquarters and Associate Chief Minister; made Shengzhou prefect Li Shenfu Huainan campaign marshal and E-yue campaign pacification commissioner, with Shuzhou training commissioner Liu Cun as his deputy; and led troops to attack Du Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial orders, Yang Xingmi promoted Zhu Jin to deputy overall commander of the eastern circuits and Associate Chief Minister, appointed Shengzhou prefect Li Shenfu as Huainan campaign marshal and pacification commissioner for the E-yue expedition with Shuzhou commissioner Liu Cun as his deputy, and marched against Du Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪將駱殷戍永興，棄城走，縣民方詔據城降。

translations.literal: Hong's general Luo Yin garrisoned Yongxing, abandoned the city and fled, and the county commoner Fang Zhao held the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong's general Luo Yin had been holding Yongxing; he fled the city, and a local man named Fang Zhao took possession of it and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「永興大縣，饋運所仰，已得鄂之半矣！」

translations.literal: Shenfu said: "Yongxing is a great county, on which transport of supplies relies—we have already gained half of E!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said, "Yongxing is a major county that feed the supply lines—we already hold half of E!"
